location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: festina lente: ascends a sculpted water groove left of the arete. short, but fun movement on unique features. might feel weird if you don't figure out the flow.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: mellow marmelade: more of a boulder problem. stick clip the first bolt then work through the perm draw to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: camp 4: good warm up for lighthouse and sandstone serenity. not hard moves just committing getting your feet onto the roof.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: they're out there: establish over an undercut roof and climb pockets and plates past a slight bulge to a horizontal break up high near the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: charred oak: the following routes are under a large roof that should keep them dry in a rain. slabby climb on decent edges that begins above a low roof and trends up and right.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: c'mon keenan: grab a few large pockets and throw big to a protrusion, figure it out past the second bolt and enjoy two mantels to the top.the grade truly depends on your height.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: go to bed jared: starts on an arching left-facing dihedral/arete feature. ascend the small dihedral then bust out right on the arete finding some helpful hidden holds. go up the arete then traverse back left on thin feet. finish on the steeper flake system above on big holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: send pickles!!: your crag snack game is just as, if not more, important than your climbing ability. send this route and treat yourself with the commonly overlooked crag snack....the baby gherkin!start on cheater stones to establish hands and initiate the classic rrg cut feet start. varied climbing of side pull pockets, slots, and ledges on a mostly vert face. finish by pulling over the top bulge and find the welcoming ledges as they become visible.even if you don't send, you should still have a pickle.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: brain fart: stick clip the first bolt and climb through small sandy holds to the ledge, continue up the corner to anchors higher up.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: minnesota  bratwurst: face climbing, ends in scoop with clip and lower draco anchors

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: jr's route: bolted pocket climb starting off a ledge on incut holds with a tricky/awkward finish. may have gotten a bit harder since some holds broke off recently.

location: Red River Gorge > Ash Branch
text: human action: the tricky arete to the ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bald Rock Cove
text: black n tan: this route serves as a good warm up for early cool days as it is in the sun in the morning, but it is also a good route in its own right. scramble up the ledge to get to the start of the route. there is an interesting undercling move to bypass a blank section. climb moderate terrain to a tough pocket sequence higher up.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bald Rock Cove
text: bald rock boogie: a little harder than the one to the left .  also a good warm up for early cool days as it is in the sun in the morning.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: gandee candy: good average 5.8 climb.  sustained, but no defined crux.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: un-koala-fied: farthest route to the left at the bears den. climb up on to a small ledge below the first bolt then work up the awkward crack and then right on good holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: silly old bear: starting right of gandee candy, follow the line of glue-ins that trend slightly right using mostly sinker pockets.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: rumspringa: start with a couple of long moves on good holds on orange rock and move up and left into a dihedral.  continue 5.9 climbing up and left until the midway point where you begin to trend right.  after clipping the last bolt traverse right under and past the chains and pull a harder move to holds from which to clip.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: c quest r: low angle route with a crux in the middle.  scramble up easy rock, pull over a small roof and power through some small pockets and slopers to a nice finish on good edges and pockets. this route tends to dry quickly because it doesn't get much runoff. it gets morning sun.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: closed - chantal's starfish: * the hangers on this route were removed in february 2019 due to the wedge bolts that were used to equip this route. it is available for rebolting if anyone wants to do it. *work you way up onto a ledge and then climb up crimps to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: ticks list: adding this because it was in our guidebook. looked like the original anchors had been removed and new ones placed down a little farther. enjoyable, easy, and short.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: golden snow cone: climb the large left leaning right facing flake to perfect pockets on the face above.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: bear goggles: start by bouldering up to a stance on the ledge above.   start into to a sea of underclings and sidepulls that will make you wander to find the path of least resistance.  finish up over a slight bulge on to larger holds to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: low hanging fruit: a nice fingery route with lots of crisp, fragile edges.  easy moves up a slab lead to a layback section below the steeper upper half.  crimp and wander up the slightly overhanging wall and then cut hard left to avoid the crack and do a few harder moves just below the anchors.  the hardest part of this route is choosing which way to go and finding the best holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Bear's Den
text: pooh and piglet too: starts behind a tree and wanders up pocket moves over a low roof to a tricky finger crack.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: grandpa joe: jugs, pockets and pinches up a vertical wall to a slab topout.  the rock is solid, the movement is fun and the bolts are safely spaced.  however, the rock becomes more sandy as the route turns slabby.  this route is still cleaning up, but once it sheds a bit more grit it will be an excellent pitch.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: chocolate river: follow the wall left of peaches and cream for about 100 yards. begin on a reachy mantel start and then climb a technical slabby face to a finish over a bulge. 50 feet, 5 bolts, rap chains does not stay dry

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: augustus gloop: a fun low-angle route.  slightly more technical than it's neighbor of the same grade, chocolate river.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: sugar rush: the leftmost of the three bolted slab routes right of "end of the innocence" (5.10b)  use finesse up the slab with a couple fun mantles and friction climbing up to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: wonkaholic: start up the low angle arete past a few holds that look like they may break.  after the start enjoy a relaxing romp past a few thought provoking sections.  the crux awaits at the top with various ways of getting to and clipping the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: throbbing emotions: 10 feet to the right of sunday night cockfights.  this route has great movement and is well protected, but needs some traffic.  start out on steep terrain to jugs right of the bolt line.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: egbg: a long fun line that begins just as you enter the left side of the chocolate factory (when the trail forks take the left side instead of the right which takes you over to oompa and loompa) one of the first climbs you will come to as you gain the cliff band. starts on large blocks under a roof. pull through the low crux to find nice long juggy climbing above with a steep finish. take time to enjoy the large sit down hueco in the center of the climb. watch for friable rock, recommend stick clipping the first bolt due to possible poor rock conditions. with more travel to clean up some of the choss i think this could be a red classic, a powerful start with a cruiser finish makes for an incredibly enjoyable way to spend a sunset at the end of the day.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: the juggernaut: starting from the ledge pull a few hard moves over the ledge on good holds. then full huge jugs to a ledge just below the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: breakin the law: start up the dirty crack or walk up and around and start off the ledge. clip the first bolt then pull a tricky roof on not as good as you would like them to be holds. the rest of the  climb is steep and deep pocket pulling!

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: three stooges: two bolts of pockets to hands-free stance, then a long rightward-traversing section of 5.8, where the biggest challenge is not z-clipping. the route earns it;'s grade near the top, where the bolts thin, and the moves lengthen.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: oompa: very nice climb, stays dry in a light rain.   start by climbing up on a flake.   continue up following pockets and plates to the top.   crux is at the point where the route starts to turn less steep, it's somewhat sequential.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: robotic thumb: a couple of thoughtful moves, using the wall to the right as needed, lead to fun climbing on a giant flake and subsequent jugs.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: grandma josephine: nice pockets and edges with a distinct section in the middle that will have you scratching your head.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: snarf victory: thoughtful and technical blunt arete climbing on less than perfect stone.  follow deep two-finger pockets and sharp edges at the start.  as the route slabs out, the holds get slopey and the movement gets more interesting.    like other routes on this outcrop, the rock slowly turns more sandy as you go up.  this route deserves way more attention than it gets.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: loompa: the sister route to oompa.  just as fun but steeper and more sequential.   good jugs and positive holds get you up to the second bolt. take time to read the holds above before heading through bolts 3 and 4. bust through the sequential crux on cool holds to even cooler holds above and lower angle climbing to the anchor.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: the glass elevator: a few easy moves off the ground get you setup for thinner crimps and balancy moves higher up. not as steep as oompa or loompa and more technical.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: babinski sign: bolted line that wraps around an arete hueco just past second bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: mr. p.: has a good amount of loose rock and fragile holds right now but has fun movement.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Chocolate Factory
text: theobroma: pull through an awkward couple of moves on good crimps to an undercling. then follow sinker pockets to a ledge. pull two roofs after the ledge and clip the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: northern nut growers association: start on either side of the crack, and ends before the ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: hazel dormouse: moderate vert climbing to a mild bulge with huge plated jugs to pull past then iron oxide holds and crimps lead to a comfy wide ledge.  using an extended draw at the 8th (ledge) bolt will help reduce rope drag.  when ready, step up off the ledge for the grand finale to a matching jug rail using subtle feet to reach giant, protruding iron oxide jugs overhead; pull yourself up and over onto an easy rock ramp to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: hazelnut: the farthest right of three routes with similar starts. this route starts on deep iron oxide pockets and plates, with enjoyable movement to a fun finish at the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: silver apples of the moon: w.b. yeats said it best in the song of wandering aengus. nature, yearning, transformation, and art. plates to slopers, overhang to slab, this route changes as much as life does.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: golden apples of the sun: the arete right of silver apples, take a bite out of this route!

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: when in drought: start just left of blunt arête angling up left on a series of plates and pockets.  head straight up past a quick crimp crux midway to a fun easy finish on a comfy ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: witch hazel: the middle of the three routes that initially climbs similarly to its two sister routes on either side then settles into cruising on beefy iron oxide ridges that thins briefly to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: hazel green: starts behind a large tulip popular tree surrounded by rhododendrons. pull-up start over a low-to-the-ground roof.  head straight up over a mild bulge in the middle eventually leading to pleasantly positive plates and a stellar juggy finish to the anchors set above a high ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hazel Hollow
text: coll: initially similar easy start as 'filbert' but then quickly departs and angles to the left towards a stance on a ledge.  pull up onto the face on slot pockets into the giant hueco on hidden jugs.  balance out on the face following jugs and sinker finger pockets before moving left again enjoying moderate climbing on comfy iron oxide ridges and plates that stays consistently good all the way to the top.

route: Hoolie Hoggin' in a Booger Hole
location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > A-Hole Wall
text: hoolie hoggin' in a booger hole: probaby the best warmup on the wall. finger friendly jugs and a moderate pump.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > A-Hole Wall
text: holey cow!: jugs but pumpy. don't let your ego get in the way and get flashed pumped.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > B-Hole Wall
text: holeshot: enjoyable climbing up the juggy arete. equipped by scott curran.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > B-Hole Wall
text: hole lot of nothing: "if you're a connoisseur of choss, step a few feet right of the arête to find this gem."climb through some bouldery moves at the start to gain much easier and slightly less dirty climbing to the top.will clean up with more traffic...maybe?

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > B-Hole Wall
text: surprise b-hole: harder start to longer pulls on good pockets and jugs. good warmup for the harder routes. equipped by scott curran

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > B-Hole Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > Hole New Wall
text: mudhole: chimney up the smooth and often wet slab using the boulder behind you. after you get past the top of the boulder the arete comes into play and the feet get a little better.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > The UnHoley Wall
text: the hole 9 yards: this is short route on nice golden rock that get's easier as you go.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Hole in the Wall > The UnHoley Wall
text: twll mawr: this route is similar in character to it's neighbor, except with a bulge to pull adds a bit of difficulty.  originally fa'd by a visiting welsh, the route name translates to "big hole".

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Leonard's Wall
text: what's new, pussycat: climb the technical vertical face as it wanders up and to the left, then pull into the chimney. the second half of the climb uses the chimney and face. excellent view at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Leonard's Wall
text: pstpstpst: start the route to the left of the first bolt where the better holds are located.  climb up to the ledge and pull a small roof. and enjoy the tricky moves to the anchors on the face. excellent view at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Leonard's Wall
text: maine coons: climb the face and choose the best line. after the ledge, enjoy the tricky run to the anchors. nice view at the top!

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Leonard's Wall
text: ten cats: start on pockets to the left of a gaping chimney. an easy first half of climbing hits a perplexing bulge at about midpoint. diagonal up and right using crimps and occasional undercling before finishing on an obvious protruding spine to the anchors.still a bit dirty with lichen and needs some traffic, but will clean up very nicely.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > Leonard's Wall
text: leonard's excellent adventure: start on 'cock rotter’s beartrap' using the first three glue-in bolts the veering left and up to an obvious hueco with chain anchors set below an orange bulge.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: festively plump: climb up a short, left-facing dihedral to gain the face. continue through horizontals and thinning pockets to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: quantity over quality: a great warmup for the wall. easy moves to a harder finish on crimps.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: awesom-o 4000: easy climbing and fun moves up the vertical face leads to a crux before the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: it's a jersey thing: start up the vertical face to the largest part of the ledge splitting the cliff. from there, climb through a discontinuous left-facing crack/dihedral feature to steeper pockets and jugs.
feature_tags: crack, dihedral, face, jug, ledge, pocket

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: about tree fiddy: an enjoyable climb unique from the rest of the wall that breaks into three distinct sections.boulder through the slopey bottom section to gain the right end of the ledge. climb through vertical, crimpy plates to another small ledge then continue up and around the arête feature to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: the dong wall: find some holds to right of the route and figure out a way to high step and get on to the ledge.  work through a series of large pockets to a somewhat spooky hollow sounding hold that seems to be ok.  lock off and grope the surprisingly sturdy large dong.  finish up on good edges and buckets.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: drugs are bad, mkay?: climb up decent holds to reach the steeper section and continue through jugs and pockets through a small roof then to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: ultravibe pleasure 2000: go through a sequence of good pockets, slots and cool rock features. enjoy a decent rest before crimping yourself up to the chains. look closely as it can be a tricky onsight.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: tears of unfathomable sadness: climb up a dirty face to the ledge below the featured overhang. pull on good holds through the steeper section until they lessen to smaller pockets. apply a bit of graceful thrutch and make your way to the chains. should clean up with more traffic.

route: A Bunch of Tree-Hugging Hippie Crap
location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > South Park
text: a bunch of tree-hugging hippie crap: start up the slab just below a protruding block. from the ledge, climb the jugs until meeting up with the left-arching flake. follow the flake up to the short roof, punch through and continue to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Motherlode > (1) Buckeye Buttress
text: the cream machine: possibly the most overlooked sport climb at the motherlode?  an interesting slab that starts in a small, vertical scoop feature and continues up debris covered, low angle rock with water grooves and edges to the top.  start on the right side of the scoop and make a few steep moves to establish yourself on some protruding edges on the left face.  a couple perplexing moves get you to a stance about 10 feet below the fourth bolt.  balance up and left along slopey water grooves then shuffle right along a juggy rail to clip(pg13 part).  mantle over the rail and continue up much easier slab using edges to the top.  i admit that this route is dirty, but the rock is great and the climbing is very fun.  might not be the best route for a budding 5.10 climber.   great option if you are looking for an adventure.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Accounting Dept.
text: shove it up your butt: the best line on the left side, follow the flake with the use of juggy pockets to perch yourself on the top pedestal. short and sweet, just watch out for that tree ;)

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Accounting Dept.
text: somehow i manage: short and punchy line for the grade, utilizes some fun pockets that look deceptively bad.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Accounting Dept.
text: two wrongs make a dwight: this route begins with the flake in the middle of the wall. between the flake and the top you’ll find yourself tackling some bouldery moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: alfredo’s pizza cafe: quick bouldery moves lead to a no hands ledge, leave the ledge with one tricky move and scramble up the iron band slab to the chains. for a bonus challenge, try clipping every bolt hands-free.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: baby back ribs: typical washed out start on sloper-plate-runnel-thingy, find the jugs and then perch yourself up a slab, couple methodical sequences towards the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: scranton, what?: easy romp up a slab, with some thoughtful moves in the upper half. still a little dirty, will clean up with traffic.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: froggy 101: float up some slab moves to the giant flake, follow the flake all the way to the top where you’ll find the anchors tucked away in the canopy. enjoy that view!

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: finer things club: scramble to the ledge, climb through the crack into a sea of side pull jugs. after resting on the last jug a long reach enters you into the techy vert business. accomplish those moves and you’ll find yourself at the anchor, and well above your last bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: rabies fun run: crux is the thin start.  meander through wavey pockets finding key holds and finish on fun flake.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: pizza by alfredo (extension): climb past the anchors of alfredo’s pizza cafe, for this punchy boulder extension. fun long reaches on iron holds lead to a sea of pockets, find the jug pockets all the way to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Dunder Mifflin
text: the electric city (extension): overhang above ‘scranton, what?’, fun reaches and technical movement make this short boulder problem exciting.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Warehouse Boulder
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Office > Warehouse Boulder
text: ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ 1: dirty and gross, idk why i bolted this

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: uncharted moss and choss: despite the unappealing name, this enjoyable climb cleaned up quite nicely and has already seen considerable traffic. pluck and plunder plentiful plump plates then balance onto the slippery slab for the finale. some underclings, sidepulls, a high foot, and a mantle move or two might be helpful.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: underclinging undertaker: on the left side of underdeveloped wall is this interesting little route that begins on a massive incut jug. climb the slab on great sidepulls and underclings up a steeping face to a wildly featured overhang with pinchy double underclings and more sidepulls. power past the overhanging finish to clip the anchors above.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unearthed mycelia: power past plentiful plates, pockets, and perhaps a possible pinch or two. fun climbing on good holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unrealistic dump truck: you definitely won't need a cdl to drive this rig. start just left of the huge beech tree, climbing up and just left of a bulge into a rare section of high-quality rock for the unlode. good plated features lead into a pocket band just before a rounded finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: undeterred: undeterred ascends the slab or flake on the right side of the wall to an overhanging pocketed section  that can be negotiated a couple of different ways depending on your reach or route reading.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unconditional: climb up the left side of the wall on mostly jugs. this line wanders past several cool holds to a neat runnel feature at the top. increasingly sandy as you get higher.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: undoubtedly, still better than trad: climb the middle section of the wall on pockets and jugs. sandy just like its neighbors, but as the fa says, "at least you're not climbing trad."

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: underestimated: mildly overhanging route with mostly good holds and a couple of big moves. it might end up feeling easier after it gets cleaned up a bit more with increased traffic.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unfulfilling: begin on the right side of the small cave and make a few steep moves to gain the face.   continue up through decent rock and good movement that unfortunately ends shortly after due to decreasing rock quality.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: undecided: this route climbs good rock and is a slightly easier version of its neighbor to the left. saunter up the slippery slab on some nice incut plates, then trend up and right making use of the limonite ledges as the route steepens.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: undetermined: plentiful plates, pockets, pinches, underclings, and an undetermined amount of uncounted and uncharted jugs will help you reach the top anchors on this slightly overhanging route.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: untoward: another 5.10 on the 5.10 wall of unlode.  climb jugs up to the next to last bolt and then cut right onto the arete as you approach the last bolt.  ride the arete using large and positive jugs that are a bit hard to see.  pull back onto the face at the anchor.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unfamilia: start by tic-tac-ing through crimps or making a long move (height-dependent) then follow slopey jugs to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unbridled: at the far left of the unlode is this sole route. it's vertical and a bit sandy due to lack of traffic. the rock quality is less than other surrounding areas but still climbable and fun.    cruise up past the first few bolts using pockets and some smaller crimps.  punch through the crux at the blank-looking-but-ultimately-more-featured-than-it-appears bulge around the fifth bolt.    grab more cool pockets to the anchor.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: undaunted: this is the 2nd from the left of the 5 routes on underdeveloped wall. begins as a mellow slab, but soon steepens and gets a bit trickier as you navigate past the overhanging bulges near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Bald Rock Recreational Preserve (BRRP) > The Unlode
text: unsung: similar to some of the nearby lines, perhaps less juggy overall and a bit of sequential pocket pulling in the middle. not that dirty for a new line at this wall, but certainly could use more traffic.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Apollo Wall
text: whistling dixie: really fun warm up route for the wall. has a steep finish to it that will leave you guessing. great lead

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > BackStreet
text: disneyland: long but juggy route. one of the longer routes at cathedral domain.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > BackStreet
text: silver spoon: it climbs like a gym route because of all the perfectly formed jugs. its only a 5.10- for the length of the route but every move is 5.8. the route follows left of the arete towards the top. the route is generously bolted (it would give old school bolters a heart attack when looking up at it from the ground).

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > BackStreet
text: mic check: currently pretty dirty but i  enjoyed the parts i put together. i think the crux is the second or third bolt then the rest of the route is pretty cruiser. ends in a short "slab". ngl the boulder at the top really freaked me out. you would never grab it but it would kill your belayer if it fell.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > BackStreet
text: 2nd wind: technical climbing with a couple boulder sections that might be considered the crux

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Left
text: tic pebble: super weird and awkward route for the grade. i absolutely loved the change in style and would suggest trying it. the crux is debatably getting to the second bolt which could be a weird fall if blown. a lot of mantling to ledges.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Left
text: stutter step: super fun route that progressively gets harder. first three bolts are pulling on jugs. last two bolts are the crux with slopers and thin crimps. its a great route for a beginning leader to learn awkward clips or a new climber to get a "harder" top rope.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Left
text: bear paw: super easy start to slabby shelves. it seems harder than the grade before you find the holds. i cleaned it oct 7 2023 so hopefully it goes easier now.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Left
text: cup a joe: super fun route but is extremely dirty currently. starts with similar overhang/lip start as open project which turns into slabby delicate moves. it might be harder than a 5.10c but is hard to tell in current state.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Right
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Backstreet-Right
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: cub scout: nice vertical to slab begginer climb, crimps and pockets positive feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: bar code: great warmup climb, some pockets and crimps fun climb for new lead climbers.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: happy girl: good warm up climb, some crimps and pockets great feet, slight slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: water to wine: great short little warm ups, wont get a better view from a climb this hieght. crimps and little lips well worth the time while your there.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: paper plate: cool short route with a low crux section that starts immediately off the ground. it has a micro overhang section. the worst part of this route is how it ends right as you are starting to get into it.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: wine to shine: short little slab line it may be a 2star climb but it has a 5 star view very much worth checking out.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: a flower of youth: crimps and ledges turns slightly slab at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: two-4-one: crimps and finger pockets, turns slight over hang at the top, dont let the lack of hieght turn you away. it is a fun and challenging climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: beans n taters: it feels like a big boulder problem. it's good rock with cool moves. the route can either be climbed right or left of the first two bolts.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: tweezer: starts with crimps, moves into some ledges, then you get into pockets and little slab up top. really fun climb amazing views from the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Blue Sky
text: better days: pockets and crimps with sime ledges and powerful moves, up top the route turns left around the corner, adds alittle excitment for the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Eden (Far Right End)
text: adam: the leftmost route that is about 10 feet shorter than "eve" to the right. face climb to a roof and climb the overhanging face to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Eden (Far Right End)
text: eve: start at the shallow dihedral and climb to the roof. pull the roof and the fun begins. fight off the pump and climb the steep rock to the higher set of anchors. super fun.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Ott's Wall
text: deere crossing: pull through a band of juggy ledges and pockets until you get to a few bolts of slab. fun for what it is, but likely to be a bit mossy and dirty until this area sees more traffic. good intro to slab though, with a few easy rrg-type moves at the start.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Ott's Wall
text: ott 2: short, dirty climb that has the same style as the rest of this crag. a few bolts of juggy sidepulls to a mossy ledge halfway up. transition to a few fun slab moves before the chains. movement is good, but the holds can be dirty and fragile on the lower section.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Ott's Wall
text: outcast: interesting side pulls and little shelves up to some fun slab moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Ott's Wall
text: ott not: pockets and interesting side pulls to get you to the slab up above. some of the holds can be fragile so check your self, just needs traffic.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Buzzards Roost > Ott's Wall
text: home drone: slightly harder than deere crossing, but similar style. the start is slightly harder to read and the rock is poorer quality in the large hueco. some great pockets get you into the slab section, which is dirtier than the route to the right, but with slightly more positive feet (depending on the footwear you've chosen).

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: rocky and bullwinkle: follow a short vertical face, around a bulge, and up good pockets and plates to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: a day late: balancy.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: pasty white: negotiate onto a neat tower to the first bolt and climb consistent pockets to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: 2 pump chump: first route on the left.  pull the roof with a helpful undercling.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: never a duhl moment: balancy and slabby, with some specific beta required to pass a relatively-featureless section.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: 6 shooter: vertical face, small bulge then ledge, then crimps to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: thumb meat: use the crack to push through a boulder problem then on to anchors

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: jersey joyride: fun crimpy route.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > East Coast Crag
text: tinder kittens: crimpy and pumpy

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Eastface
text: first light: decent lead for a beginner climber looking for either a redpoint or onsight. i'd suggest new climbers to stick clip the first bolt due to low crux.starting moves follows shallow crack with awkward feet. follow slab sequence to large ledge. pull though slight overhang to ending easy slab sequence.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Eastface
text: handsight: good route with pumpy ending to chains

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Eastface
text: sink or swim: good route but needs thorough cleaning before it can reach its true potential. the starting 2 bolts were the crux for me but it might be because of the bad feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Hades
text: have mercy: basically a warm up route for the wall its shorter than most but it will serve its purpose well.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Inner Loop Trail > Patterson
text: higher ground: climbs better than it looks. it has fun moves and would be a great first lead.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Inner Loop Trail > Patterson
text: butterscotch: a straightforward and well protected climb. mostly vertical or slightly less than vertical, with a small overhang towards the top. the beginning is quite chossy, but will improve with time as the line sees more traffic. beware of loose rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Inner Loop Trail > Patterson
text: the birthing: start in an alcove and stem up the chimney that narrows to a squeeze where you get "birthed". fun route that departs from cookie cutter face routes. when it starts feeling hard look around.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Inner Loop Trail > Patterson
text: rocky road: thought provoking route with fun moves on mostly vertical rock. just right of "the birthing"

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > K9 Crag
text: fudge: fun short route. it had interesting moves for how easy it was. clipping the first bolt is a must since you could tumble down the hill into the metal rungs that lead to big wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > K9 Crag
text: stoop dog: bouldery overhanging start leads to fun climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > K9 Crag
text: flea bitten stranger: the route starts just left of the corner and climbs up the overhanging face arete to a dihedral. figure out the bouldery crux to gain the arete and then save your energy for the crazy fun finish at the top that liebacks the corner crack to the anchors. the guide says 5.9+ but it may seem harder depending on your reach.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > K9 Crag
text: in dog years: trail ends directly under this overhanging jug fest with a roof about 15 feet off the ground.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > K9 Crag
text: dawgillhunt: starts with stemming and briefly follows crack. it's continuous tedious slab to top. the guide calls it a 5.10b but it feels harder. the bolts are really generous and well placed so it shouldn't intimidate someone that is getting into slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Knowhere Wall
text: lost: crux will be getting off the ground. start with some small crimps and throw for a ledge. cake walk after that.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Knowhere Wall
text: tunnel vision: some funky moves lead to more funky moves

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Knowhere Wall
text: borrowed time: climb a short face to some anchors. weird funky movement

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Ladder Horn Wall
text: spoiled: good first 5.10 lead, short line but very consistent climb. technical climbing pockest great stone.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Ladder Horn Wall
text: bull legged: short line but will challenge you if given the chance. small little finger pockets and crimps

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Left Box
text: peace time: short and sweet. would be a good intro to climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Left Box
text: jabba: jugs for days.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Light House Crag
text: the beacon: low crux. short but sustained vertical climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Light House Crag
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Litter Box > Lower Tier
text: pulse: this route is like a beginner friendly version of some of the rest of the crag. it climbs a lot like a gym route. a nice amount of pinches, a couple of slopers, and very solid clips for a new leader.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Litter Box > Lower Tier
text: lockjaw: difficult getting off the ground, but eases significantly once you are.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Litter Box > Lower Tier
text: evidence of overeating: debatably the easiest 5.10c i’ve ever climbed(weird for how stiff cathedral can be). first two bolts are 5.5 climbing to v2/3 crux move on bolt 3. the rest of the route is a cruiser jugfest to the anchor. multiple no hands rests.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Moon Wall
text: comith alive: ledges and pockets. slight overhanging sections of climbing. climb just to the left of the roof gets alittle more height then the 5.9 to the right.very fun climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Moon Wall
text: aunt betty's bic ups: very fun climb lips and pockets great hands good rock, overhanging

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Moon Wall
text: will'd power: climbs just to right of the roof still has some steep to it but not like the others 10c climb with a couple 10d boulder problems has these iron rails that run throughout the route.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Pumpkin Patch
text: sunday funday: nice easier lead. some low-angle climbing for the first few bolts, then a bit of a juggy traverse and the up to the anchors. fun.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Pumpkin Patch
text: pumpkin 3.14: slightly harder than sunday funday, it's nice easy and fun stuff. trend slightly to the right after a ledgy start. shorter climbers may struggle reaching the permadraws to clip the chains.when wet (or after recent rain) the finish jug can be very wet, but the hold is so good it shouldn't be an issue (except some muddy fingers!)

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Pumpkin Patch
text: flying nun: plate pulling on a slight overhang. some fun moves down low take you to the cruxy mantle. a long reach and then jugs to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Pumpkin Patch
text: holly berry: a very nice route for your first 10a lead.a fun (cruxy) ledge pull after the first bolt (well protected). the rest is fun climbing with multiple good rests.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Pumpkin Patch
text: elevado: great route for the length, crux might be the shelf, has some big moves. will leave you wanting more!

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Somewhere
text: everywhere: it felt like a gym route with with all the conveniently placed jugs. great lead for a beginner. easy clipping holds and cool movement. the first bolt is the "crux".

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Somewhere
text: anywhere: tricky thin start, kicks back slightly near the end.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Somewhere
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Somewhere
text: here: it is here. first route on wall(has a small sign.) short technical climb with slab start that continues to slight overhang.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Sun Wall
text: killing the blues: thin little ledgs going from slab to vert pretty quick. then gets steeper but good pockets some good rests before you push for the chains. great first 5.10 lead great protection and positive holds good rests just a great route.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Sun Wall
text: full mac: a great route starts kinda thin til a little ledge from there, great holds has some pokects and good rest before you hit the slight overhang.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Sun Wall
text: orange crush: this could be one of the best routes at the domain in my opinion,  some pockets and crimps. but the exposure makes it feel harder. and the height of the route is incredible you start climbing above the tree line, just incredible veiw.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Sun Wall
text: bruised not broken: tricky slab to start then gets in to ledges and pockets turns overhang for the last bolts very well protected. fun route.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Sun Wall
text: special tea: technical slab, to vertical good rest on a ledge starts to get steeper as you climb some interesting shifts of the body make it a little more tricky up top but a amazing route.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > The Port
text: slow rider: starts on a slight ledge, line runs just to the left of this little whole in the rock you can climb into for a rest if desired

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Westside
text: beach front: very crumbly rock; very sandy; covered in moss.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Westside
text: sand castle: very crumbly rock; very dirty/sandy; covered in moss.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Westside
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Westside
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: shaming: powerful start great holds gets thin in the 4th 5th bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: dope sick: great climb, very commiting start, crimps and some interesting side pulls, positive holds interesting finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: system failure: these little lips and rails that run throughout. with some pockets.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: sunny side up: great route with some interesting whole/little seats half way up the route. pockets and crimps. can through in a knee bar on the left side of the first whole.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: 2 lefts aint right: high feet to start small ledges or rails then pockets

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: temet nosce: hard start with interesting hand placement and directional holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > Gypsy Camp
text: grilled cheese: crimps and some pockets with a good rest at the 4th bolt.vertical technical climbing

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > The Metro
text: milk money: offers an interesting variety of movement start to finish.  start in a very wide dihedral on mellow slab layback to a sitdown rest.  next, use ample jugs to move up the small roof; when the jugs run out, figure out the mantel crux .  finish with a couple effortless bolts before deciding how you need to clip the anchors. drop-ins at top.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > The Metro
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > [Redacted]
text: middle man: thin pinches and crimps through the first couple bolts then you get in to some pockets with a ledge in the middle.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > White Pine Trail > [Redacted]
text: vaya con todos: cool route with a two sections of contrasting styles - low, thin/pinchy crux gets you to two bolts worth of big pockets at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Wind Tunnel
text: a shadow in the wind: a great route if you looking to start leading 5.10, a very consistent climb

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Wind Tunnel
text: recurve: starts off a little tuff but gets easier at the top, also a great route for someone just starting to lead climb 5.10

location: Red River Gorge > Cathedral Domain > Wind Tunnel
text: ground zero: fun little route, will get in you mind a little at the top

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Alcatraz
text: traumatized turtle: adventurous route up large ledges to a low angled face

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Alcatraz
text: sweet petunia: traverse right on a dirty start. similar difficulty as the sport line immediately to the left.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Alcatraz
text: man with a wooden leg: after stickclipping the first bolt, amble rightwards into a large hueco.  pull the roof on good holds of marginal integrity (crux) to get established on the face above.  once established more enjoyable climbing with a wide variety of holds on a slightly overhanging face leads to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: see you on thursday: this line of easy climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: castle awed: this line is very similar to and within eyesight of see you on thursday.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: ralfe the wonder llama: a few feet to the right is this obvious slab. take your time to find your way through a mix of holds to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: european swallow: look to the right of holy grail. there is a short bolted line. this is a vertical line with a cruxy 2nd bolt move.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: the snows of winter: slab route to the right of the swallows

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: arthur, king of the britons: climb the short featured face to a mantle at the ledge above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: trojan rabbit: follow the to right and look for a blunt arete. after a cruxy start move on jugs to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: the keeper: enjoy an easy slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: english pip dogs: another 100 feet right takes you to a straight vertical wall. this route has a cruxy start (potentially hard for short people). get through this and you have even climbing to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: ham and jam and spam: the crux is above the last bolt. jam your right hand in the crack, find good feet, and clip the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: lady of the lake: turn the corner and find the best part of camelot. this is the first of 3 routes on the tall wall. either start on the overhang directly below the 1st bolt or traverse in from the right. enjoy the vert/techy sequences.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: she's a witch: except for the crux at the start this is almost a twin to lady of the lake. after the crux at the 2nd bolt enjoy the big holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: roger the shrubber: starting on the right side of the ledge and left of the tree, move up and left through the cruxy first 2 bolts to a ledge. continue with a few reachy moves on good edges to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: siege perilous: a thrilling route offering goods rests in between sparse, technical sections. a comfortable sit-down rest awaits at the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: brave sir robin: start on the flake/slab. after the no hands rest get through the fingery section to finish on jugs. this route would not be suitable for a top rope because of rope drag at the anchors. it is slightly overhung. when danger reared its ugly head he quickly turned his tail and fled.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: the enchanter: this a short slab. the crux is finding the holds. they are there. be patient.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: holy grail: this is the most beautiful line at camelot and the vision of josephine sterr who with jesse started the development of this crag. if you like you can climb the first half of it (5.9) to a set of anchors and lower.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: a herring: bring a stick clip! you must climb the jug overhaul and cut down the mightiest tree with... a herring! equipped by jesse sterr

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Camelot
text: your mother was a hamster: be ready for some thin crimps in the middle.  the holds can be hard to find toward the top, making the route feel harder than the moves actually are.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Chaos
text: lithuanian princess: a hard move off the ground leads to better holds but an extremely pumpy face for the grade above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Chaos
text: raise hell: after finishing the enjoyable climbing on lithuanian princess, continue climbing through dirty ledges and a thorn bush to finish the climb on plates.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Chaos
text: slabalicious: starts on a few vertical ledgy moves up to a black slab. use the arete to pull through the crux or some tricky calf burning shenanigans. ends on a surprisingly bad ledge. usually wet.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Chaos
text: die with a blessing: this line starts with a hard move off the top of the boulder (be sure to stick clip it) to great movement on small edges to a bit of crux about three quarters of the way up. the slightly overhung face is sure to pack a bit of a punch.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Cloud 9
text: rough around the edges: steep easy jugs but with a lot of holds still breaking. not bad but you've been warned.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Cloud 9
text: liftoff: less steeper than the routes to the right but still the bouldery start the red is known for. slab crux in the middle.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: sending in the rain: a short blank section down low requires a bit of lock off and reach. then enjoy relaxed and casual climbing above with plenty of good holds and rests to choose from.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: feets don't fail me now: start left of the first bolt to take advantage of some back stepping on the wall behind you then trust your feet on the slab run to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: skull eyeland: its mostly easy slab except for a bouldery move at the 4th bolt as you leave the midway ledge. then a little cryptic at the last bolt but a well protected crux.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: nystagmus: pull over  roof then climb up small pockets and edges to a balancy crux near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: la nambla: this route climbs up interesting pockets and edges. slightly dirty now but should clean up nicely.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: grain of salt: not the best route on the wall. funky and slightly pumpy climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: road kill: hard moves lead to a sit down rest in a hueco before a pumpy run to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: grab n' go: fun jug hauling to an interesting tongue of rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: where the sidewalk ends: well flowing moves from bottom to top. good'ish rests to keep the pump at bay but if you can't figure them out, good luck

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: lit mini kart: start on the first few holds of diesel therapy then head up and right. 5.10 pump leads to a fun run to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Coopers Cove
text: all washed up: climb edges up a slightly less than vertical face.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Corner Pocket
text: nobody cares: walk left and uphill about ten feet to start and angle up and right to the first bolt. keep angling slightly right for the first three bolts and follow the well featured slab to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Corner Pocket
text: elevator pitch: start with an easy boulder problem then follow deep jugs until a slight pumpy section near the top. great warm-up route for the other routes at this crag.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Corner Pocket
text: friends fur life: this is a new route immediately to the right of elevator pitch. the rock at the base of the climb with the name and possible grade suggests 5.10d. this seems correct given that the hand and feet holds currently crumble underneath you as you climb. once this route is cleaned up, it may be a little easier (10c? 10b?). climb it! this will be a great route once some of the choss has been knocked off.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Deep End
text: the salty dawgs: shares the first bolt with half mast then veers right on glue-ins up the brief slab section to a secondary ledge. cruise up the jug-covered face and pull into a small alcove at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Deep End
text: fluffer: route just right of pool boy.  technical climbing on underclings and pockets.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Deep End
text: pool boy: the long climb that begins just right of the mungy crack on the right side of the crag.  pumpy climbing on underclings and pockets leads to a tough redpoint crux guarding the chains.  best warmup at the crag.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Deep End
text: the cough: walk out on the narrow ledge to the pile of cheater stones. stick clip first bolt and go big for the horizontal break in the wall. crank steep, fun moves through the roof that end all too soon as you enjoy cruiser terrain to the anchors slightly left of the line.   the belayer should clip into the fixed rope at the base and the climber should stay trammed in on the rope to get back to the ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: poppin cherries: blocky not great climbing. not the best route on the wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: banana split: blocky climbing to a bit of a run out to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: first date: a nice warm up. start on an interesting left hand pinch thing and make a hardish move off the ground then follow jug plates to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: strawberry fields: boulder the start and enjoy tufa-like pinches. a little chossy right now, but should clean up to be a good route. optional extension (lucy in the sky) to take the route to 11b. good view from the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: jewjew fruit: climb a finger crack to start rest on the ledge then fire up the beautiful golden face to a pumpy finish

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: heath ledger: one of the coolest looking routes at fruit wall. it looks like the cliff melted over to the right. a slightly bouldery start leads to a lot of ledges and jugs. pull over some jugs and finish on some fancy slab to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: bovine stimulator: sequential true slab climbing on slimpers and iron oxide pockets. shares anchors with disco strangler.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: melon baller: good vertical climbing on a variety of holds.  high step to get started moving up on horizontal bands.  follow a vertical crack for two bolts before encountering a crimpy crux on small edges and narrow slots before gain jugs and lower angle rock to the finish.  still pretty sandy right now but should clean up for a solid 10+.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Fruit Wall
text: lichen lessons: climb up through a featured face to a small roof. pull the roof and climb through some thin, pocketed crux to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Highlands
text: goose bumples: start off the ledge on lower-angle rock then follow the fat flake feature into the upper, pocketed headwall. watch out for the sneaky pump at the end if you can't find the right holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: devotion: keep your balance as you scramble up the slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: confessional: ponder your transgressions as you make it to the last bolt crux, then reach for absolution at the anchors that are shared with the trad climb to the left.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: slabsinthe: put on your best slab sending shoes, take a sip of your favorite beverage and pray you don’t slip getting to the first bolt. then enjoy the ample ledges to the top.

route: Twist your Hip and do the Dip
location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: twist your hip and do the dip: a short vertical climb.  start on thin crimps as a stem or with terrible feet on the face as the originals have exfoliated and move up to a shallow hueco with a good move off an undercling.  continue up on decent crimps to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: pickled pig's feet: longest line on the wall.  step lightly on some frail appearing holds with thin moves through the first few bolts.  grab an undercling below the bulge looking inside first to avoid a buggy surprise to reach jugs and the final run to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: thelonius: an easy looking slab has the crux down low between the 2nd and 3rd bolts. continue past a bulge at the 4th bolt to finish on more slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: sugar pad: pretty much straight up vertical with good finger ledges.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: narcissus: starts as a slab and finishes as vert. well bolted.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: monks brew: traverse in from the ledge or stick clip and boulder up from ground on some sandy rock to reach the main face.  make some long reaches on good holds on the vertical face before tackling the overhang as the climb trends up and right into a black streak.  grab a shake at the last bolt before the final few moves to the chains as hanging the draws on the anchor may be the crux for some.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: snug: start on crimps and balance your way up to a large hueco. continue up on better holds to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Monastery
text: goldmund: bolted route on the arete. mellow start up to a ledge, followed by the crux on a bulging section a bit to the right. it eases up a bit on varied terrain from there to the top.

text: one feeling: start under the small roof. climb plates to the anchors. stays wet from the last bolt to anchor as top drains. be mindful of the tree, it was here first. but because fairies were so small, they were only big enough for one feeling at a time.

text: a tarantella: count in on the cheater stones on the left side of the arête. this song is good for thinking.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: lost marbles: furthest route on the left. grab those slopey marbles and ricochet to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: NA

text: english gentlemen don't beg: please! leftmost route on the next section of the wall. starts with a short overhang, and maintains its dignity the rest of the way up.

route: If You Were Me, I'd Be Ugly
location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: if you were me, i'd be ugly: fun moves on solid edges. stays wet with the last couple of bolts as top land drains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: the unruly shadow: never does what it should, but we still love it. climbs to the left of the tree. low crux and thoughtful movement.

route: To Live Would Be An Awfully Big Adventure
location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: to live would be an awfully big adventure: other side of the tree, this route tackles the bulge at the 4th bolt. tons of rests in between moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: something worser: what could be worse than being shot at by pirates? my thoughts... aren't... very... happy! iron oxide ridges up the path of least resistance.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: noodler: this fearsome pirate, with his hands on backwards, starts on the right side of the ledge in the crack. iron oxide ridges lead to a slabby finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: NA

text: many different kinds of brave: this route is the center line on the face.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: oh, the cleverness of me: next three routes are on a ledge off an approach trail. this is the leftmost line on this section of the wall and starts on a boulder, up a chossy break to the face.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: NA

route: Never is an Awfully Long Time
location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: never is an awfully long time: the arête start to access the ledge was an afterthought. start there, or clamor around to the right side of the boulder and access the ledge under "noodler." stick-clip off the ledge and head up the center of the wall. will feel easy for the grade for tall climbers, harder if you are shorter than 5'5".

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: bill jukes: every inch of this route is covered in tattoos and starts on the next ledge. crimpy cruxes will keep you thinking. wet after rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: tick tock: starts just to the left of a small cave feature. right leaning route six feet right of 'fairies.' the anchor positioning is not good for top roping.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: old, alone, done for: if you don't get the crux, we'll feed you to the crocodile. the wall hosting these next three climbs stays damp for a while after rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Neverland
text: mr. smee: you've got to have a cool head to work with hook and stay alive. seems tender at first, but really tough as nails.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: sterling moss: smear through dirt and moss to a cleaner headwall. utilize the side of the crack and tech your way up to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: plate for the party: starts of a cheater stone uphill of synthetic, roof start to cool plates.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: alpha dog: just before the obvious dihedral up on the nice ledge system. delicate crux to an unexpected pump. bring a brush to love this one into shape.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: castaway: starts a few few feet right of the obvious omega dihedral from a small pedestal. interesting plates and crimps lead up a beautiful licheny pillar of rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: reality check: follow the arete up past some steep moves. jugs are right where you need them.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: for real: start ten feet right of the arete and climb on small ledges past a small bulge near halfway to a slab finish

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: deep state: start up through some small fingertip jugs to small ledges with some technical moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: lichening bolt: iron ledges led to a slight bulge in the middle, then cruise to the end.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: turd burglar: another interesting moderate on the plated face right of poop chute.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: surrealistic pillow: starts left of a big chossy hole in the wall and climbs to a ledge at the first bolt, then through a series of technical mini ledges with an occasional side pull.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: inscrutable: starts on the right side of a slabby wall. head to a ledge and small roof past the first bolt, then make some technical moves past a bulge and up into slab territory near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: hunkered down: climb past a bulge to thin ledges and a tricky finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: the darkening: make your way up a short flake to thin technical ledges above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: depth charge: mostly slabby but with a variety of underclings and side pull moves to keep the grade down. ledge between 1st and 2nd bolts has some sandy spots but the working holds are good.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: hammer and butterfly: climb the iron ledges to just before the third bolt, then tackle hard moves possibly including some chimney action in the wide crack.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Real Deep End
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: nursery time (aka battery): this is the middle line of bolts left of the beaver patrol crack.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: path of virtue: climb up on a ledge via 5.5 boulder on the right side.  walk across ledge, clip into fixed anchor.  this climb is the furthest climb on the left side of the ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: chopped: start from on top of a boulder and pull a couple of moves to mantle up to a ledge. from here, take the right path and continue to trend right on gym like jugs that should put a smile on your face.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: bailey: begins on a corner 20 feet to the left of victory sip and shares the first bolt with barnum. after the first bolt climb up and right through a series of bulges on jugs and plates.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: road to debauchery: good ol' fashioned link-up lets you skip the low crux. start on path of virtue and cut left to finish on victory sip after the 3rd bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: short list: pull yourself up on jugs to a no hands stance. then reach high for some grips that will help you get through the hardest moves on the route. if you can't reach those holds, you may find yourself joining the short list of people who won't enjoy this route. enjoy the juggy run to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: don quixote: start on the right side of this wall, climb up and leftward through the cruxy lower half to gain the ledge after the second bolt. then cruise up the slab to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: sting: fun moderate climbing with a couple of moves to keep you honest. skirt the right side of the large hueco and finish on steep jug pulling. continue past the anchors of sting for a step up in difficulty. work through a some so-so crimps while trending left to the anchors. currently a bit run out but a bolt will be added in the future. if you find a bolt in between , consider yourself lucky. (stung 5.11b, 80ft. 8 bolts fa ian kirk, 2016)

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Sanitarium
text: chossfit: a bouldery start gives way to fun climbing on a nice mix of jugs and edges. a cable is available to keep you on the ledge while you get to the route and a belay station is at the base.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Scotch Wall
text: auchentoshan: start with some high hand holds and bad feet, climb the vertical face on technical crimps.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Scotch Wall
text: peat monster: technical vertical climbing on a striking wall with several huecos. pull off the ground with a few physical moves, then crimp your way through thoughtful climbing with the occasional good rest. big holds for the last 15ft take you to the chains at the top of the cliff.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Scotch Wall
