text: glenmorangie: climb up the corner, being wary of chossy feet to the right. follow good edges and crimps up the face, making the right decisions on which way to go when the holds diverge.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Scotch Wall
text: kilt or be kilt: climb up easy lichen-y rock to a slabby crux at 5th bolt. balance your way through big moves on small crimps and be rewarded with easy climbing to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: little wing: climb through an awkward start on slightly slopy holds to a layback crack up to a large ledge. continue above the ledge on good crimpy plates to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: hippie lip balm: a few hard moves to get off the ground followed by nicely featured slab. if you use the tree it is 5.7 but without the tree seemed more like 10b. great climbing and fun moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: nilbog night life: interesting slab climbing. starting with weird moves up the runnel to weird reaches and moves above. very clean solid rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: going away party: great break into the 10's. follow trail left to hippie lip balm, then trek about 15 feet up the steep incline on the right.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: the net: tough near the bottom a bit left of an orange dihedral, followed by edge climbing to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: geezer pleaser: despite the name, this is one of the best easier routes at secret garden.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: inside job: pull onto the wall over a cave and climb through and initially thin section in order to gain a large break. climb the featured face above to a flake system that trends right then straight up; follow this to the chains.enjoyable climbing and well-bolted for novice leaders.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: ae911truth: grab a nice, fat, square flake to get to the first bolt then shift right. play around in a pair of huecos in the middle of the wall after which the angle kicks back a bit.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: cock to the rock: begin on a dirt ledge and pull up onto a stepped rock ledge to gain the face. pull a difficult low move then cruise up the slab passing a trio of shallow huecos. stick clip the second bolt if you want to be super safe.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: rethink911: technical slab climbing with several interesting moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: rememberbuilding7: starts slabby then moves to vertical crimpy face moves up the beautiful face above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: controlled demolition: mount the ledge above the first bolt then climb extremely easy juggy slab up the orange face until it gradually gets steeper and you are wishing for those giant jugs you were on before. find  couple great holds and clip the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: at what cost: start up on the grassy ledge and find good holds on the edge of the rock ledge. lift up to the small hueco and use the edges of the brief crack to get to the jug. shake out for a second then get high feet to make the reach up to a subtle but decent crimp rail. gain footing and reach up again to a smaller but closer crimp rail. once through that, it's smooth sailing on progressively larger holds to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Secret Garden
text: salsa brava: climb through a few ledges to meet a slab face.  conquer the small technical roof following the bolted line, no deviations (go left from bolt 3 to 4). enjoy a full rest to then wrap it up with  some technical slab moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Serenity Point
text: fodiqua: excellent slab climbing up the quickly cleaning up face. crux is near the beginning but mostly consistent at the grade.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Serenity Point
text: linny lu: climb the crimpy face to a small crux near the roof to a easy ride to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Serenity Point
text: dancing queen: this line climbs up the slightly less than vertical face on good crimps. power through the low crux to more relaxed climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Serenity Point
text: trigger finger: slab technical climb with a steeper finish. the crux offers a unique rare hold that grants the route's name. beginner kneebar bonus.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Serenity Point
text: dirty habit: pull the initial moves of undercut, slightly sandy rock. one established on the vertical face, move up while trending left a bit to gain the arête. climbing the arête, or just right of it, past five or six bolts to a great recovery stance. then pull up the steeper arête, past one great jug, to another small stance just before the final little headwall. stay strong and finish up by moving left to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Hal Garner Memorial Crag
text: unknown: pockety throughout most of the route.  slabby finish without much to hold.  very chossy at the top, making the finish much harder than it would be otherwise.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Hal Garner Memorial Crag
text: halphabet soup for the soul: right end of the wall after approaching.  climb to the right of the hueco.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: wheelchair access: fun slab with a bulge crux near the anchors

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: temperature rising: this route is mostly slab. there is a puzzling bulge at the second bolt with a bit of runout to the third bolt. there is an easier bulge at fourth bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: recooperate: a short route near the right end of the crag that heads up a right-facing flake. this route has cleaned up since it was bolted and the movement is nice!

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: calling out sick: start the route out by using a crimp and choosing between mostly poor feet with one very cool iron ball foothold. once through this section you will enjoy a romp up to a bulge that provides the crux and a very interesting sequence to gain the wall above. utilize your slab skills and scamper up towards the anchors while enjoying cool holds and a great view. longer than you would expect from the ground.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: typhoid mary: climb right leaning arete to the first set of anchors. if it's dry, climb to the second set of anchors going at 5.11d

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: aquagenic urticaria: start on good holds making its way into the small open book on small nubs. continue up with a hard move into the hueco above that you clip from.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: recovery room: once a bit of a sandy pile this has cleaned up into a great route. start from the left under recooperate and traverse in. make moves to gain the ledge above then pull a small roof to huge jugs going all the way to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: 98.6: work up to a tiny ledge after the second bolt and traverse a couple feet left, then angle up and left to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: zoonotic: start with some fingers in two pockets and make some bouldery moves. if it's raining, rest assure that wet streaks don't touch the good holds necessary to put this climb in the bag.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Infirmary
text: pre-op: this climb has some incredibly sharp holds that will probably not hurt so bad after some traffic. if you love super sharp holds that destroys skins and bites back, get on it and tick it off.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Laboratory
text: devil's glen: somewhat of a warm up for the wall.  an awkward start leads to more enjoyable climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Morgue
text: last gasp: start by climbing up through some chossy rock to slightly better rock and a challenging move above the third bolt.  be prepared for some runout sections on less than vertical terrain with dirty and friable rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Nursery
text: pixadoodle: climb up between hazy dazy and a hueco. (this is the second route from the left on the slab wall.)

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Nursery
text: end of state maintenance: start on the overhung face and get your money's worth for the grade in the first 10 feet. recommend stick clipping the first bolt if you're not solid on 11s. after that just pumpy and fun moves to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Nursery
text: southern satisfaction: start just right of end of state maintenance. some big moves to good holds lead to a ledge. pull the final bulge on big holds to an anchor at the lip.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Nursery
text: the sierra alta shuffle: bouldery start into good jugs some good rests then thins out at the top

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Pharmacy
text: chasing butterflies: start by climbing by climbing dirty slightly chossy rock to gain the slab face. crimp down hard through a tough crux and finish on easier slab climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Pharmacy
text: the hairy caterpillar: access the base by walking in across the mossy slab and onto a narrow, vegetated ledge. start through dirty, sandy, chossy rock on the initial section of vert. mantel onto the slab and tech up past a crux and other thoughtful sequences. be ready to make a couple moves a little ways above a few of the bolts

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Playpen
text: dirty diaper: short and dirty may never clean up. crux will be clipping the anchor from a dirty ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Playpen
text: spank the baby: lots of easy edges with a tough crimp midway. get a left hand on a good crimp get feet high and if your short throw big with the right and spank the baby.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: zero gravity: short juggy route on the far left side of the portal.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: circle the wagons: start up the same green bottom as its neighbor to the left, but climb the right slab. it might be graded easier, but be prepared to get creative on this one.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: state of affairs: lieback up a chossy flake and stand on the ledge below the slab. venture up on sparse holds, making use of the arête and smearing feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: trouble afoot: scramble up the moss-covered bottom to a small ledge. edge and smear your way up using more real slab technique than you're probably used to in the red.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: time wrinkle: bouldery start with weird crux at 2nd bolt

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: barefoot barrista: classic slab movement all the way with a committing move near the last bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Portal
text: tesseract: looks can be deceiving and while this route may appear short and easy, it is quite pumpy. begin with a high step and follow the line of the bolts that trend right. avoid climbing into the choss up and left by staying closer to the bolt line.  a final hard pull off a left hand sidepull at the last bolt requires a little oomph right when the pump is really kicking in.  despite only a moderate amount of vertical gain, the amount of traversing and overhang really add to the distance covered on this route.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Record Shop
text: bangerz: use the cheater stones to gain the face pull a hard move to the first bolt (stick clip recommended) then follow much easier moves over a small roof to the anchors. big holds seem to be every where.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Record Shop
text: call me maybe: this route shares the start and the first bolt with bangerz. after the initial hard start continue on huge fun holds. the route move to being a bit less than vertical towards the top and uses large slopers to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > The Record Shop
text: pet sounds: this route starts with a hard boulder problem near the second bolt then moves higher to easy moves on huge jugs with a bit of spice to the bolt spacing. finish on a sweet move around an arete to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Miller Fork Recreational Preserve (MFRP) > Vine Wall
text: grandpa philly: start off to the right side for an easier start and work your way up a nice dihedral with good feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Animal Crackers Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Animal Crackers Wall
text: casey: crimpy for 45 feet, then pure friction and balance for the next 30 feet to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Animal Crackers Wall
text: panda bear: this is the first route encountered on the slabby animal crackers wall. crimps on a slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Animal Crackers Wall
text: sam: if you approach this route with the mindset that nothing at a wall named animal crackers could quite possibly be difficult then you may get smacked down by this tough little slab. best route on the wall.

route: The Short, Happy Life of Francis Macomber
location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bibliothek
text: the short, happy life of francis macomber: worth doing if for nothing else than to get used to the rock here- an engaging start through the first two bolts leads to easy climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: sweet jane: formerly one of the few interesting trad lines at bruise brothers, sweet jane has now been retrobolted as a somewhat less remarkable sport route.  follow a somewhat broken and nicely-featured dihedral up to a short left-leaning hand crack toward the top.  pull the crack and finish at the anchors under the big roof.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: the bee's business: fun bolted route just to the left of sweet jane. climbs a little bit easier and is a little more fun than sweet jane.  according to jeff colombo, the route got it's name from the large bees nest that usually forms near the bottom of the route each summer. glad i was there in the spring!

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: put the best foot forward: easy trad romp to the disconnected blocks below the two bolts.  mantle the ledge.  clip the bolts and head to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: redeye brew: solid pockets and very nice underclings climb to a nice top out on a large ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: trundling kentucky: this route has a little of everything from face moves, jugs and a mantle to get you to the anchors. clip the anchors high and to the left on the ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: ohio climbing: climb large plates and pockets to a short crux near the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: blue ridge crew: climb the gray face right of redeye brew on mostly good holds with a few thin ones sprinkled into the mix.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: send me on my way: feels easier than 5.9, easy clipping stances, nice jugs.  very good climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: flutterby blue: traverse in to the arete from either side, or attempt the bouldery, reachy direct start for bonus points and a jump in the difficulty rating. then go up.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: petrichor: begin on the vertical orange face down and left of redriveroutdoors. stick clip the high first bolt then aim for the notch in the triangular shaped roof above. the roof can be climbed to the left or the right of the second bolt. make the roof moves and cruise up the juggy slab and dihedral.
feature_tags: cruise, dihedral, face, jug, roof, slab

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: gobblers of geosmin: this route cleaned up nicely and has some interesting holds and movement. establish yourself on the initial bulge and stretch to the arching “c” shaped crack. continue up and right to reach two more bolts and the top anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: overseer: this mildly overhanging sport route begins from the left edge of the ledge up and right of “rat stew”. positive plates, incut edges, juggy sidepulls, and an occasional pocket will lead you to a scenic spot that oversees the main bruisebrothers wall. fun and flowy climbing with excellent exposure. please be cautious when stick clipping the first bolt. a future belay bolt might be helpful here. stays dry in the rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: stay off the radio jeff!: this route is the bolted line to the left of bee's business. ascend a slabby section to a small roof, navigate the roof and continue up the slab to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: rat stew: nice moderate sport route.  climb up the low-angle slabby start on balancy little knobs.  then climb up the steeper upper wall using good big holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: little viper: start on a right-facing flake, then pull boulder problem through the roof, and up easier ground to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: guardians of gaia: surmount the bulge at the first bolt with the help of a slopey sidepull pinch. the route eases up after the first bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: beta bros: right of beta babes is beta bros. bouldery beginning with a flake feature to a big or burly bump move. juggy jaunt from there to clip the chains. stays dry in the rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: critters on the cliff: a lower-angle slabby start gives way to a steeper upper wall.  climb through a short section of overhanging thin crack and continue to the chains using big holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: hey there, fancy pants: start by climbing up a flake to slightly easier ground above.  good fun.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: workin' for the weekend: climb the moderate slab to get to the first crux section as the wall steepens... this crux can be done to the right of the bolt (techy) or the left (powerful) at about the same grade... above this you get a little rest the one more crux pulling an overlap and through a notch(an undercling may help)... from there it eases up a bit till you are at the chains...

route: Don't Take Yer Guns to Town
location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: don't take yer guns to town: the guidebook calls this a "one-move wonder," but if you don't have some gas left to get to the anchors after the roof, your next move will be straight down.  starting at a short dihedral, climb up and right to easy ground that leads up to a roof.  clip the bolt on the lip, then hand-traverse right before making a reachy move to pull the roof (crux).  continue straight up past the last bolt to anchors that are invisible until you're almost on top of them.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: beta babes: this short, but steep route has a few powerful moves and long reaches on mostly good holds. it may only be 30 ft, but it overhangs 10 ft and packs a punch. stays dry in the rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: goblins of gombe: right of “guardians of gaia” is another route that has a slopey crux at the first bolt. this one is a bit more desperate and requires some technique and balance along with some sloper squeezing.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Bruise Brothers Wall
text: return of manimal: climb a low-angle slabby start to the more vertical wall.  ascend the steeper via reachy moves and big holds to the roof just before the anchors.  pull through the roof to arrive at the chains.  good route.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: manteleer: the route follows a small dihedral then goes up to the left. this route is not straight forward but is very enjoyable

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: acme corporation: climb the pocketed face between a small arete feature and another arete to the right using plentiful pebbly pockets with many helpful underclings along the way.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: wile e. coyote: a reachy start leads to juggy pockets and sidepulls. finish on a short overhanging section using a massive hidden jug to clip the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: thunderclinger: this is a fun little climb that is both dynamic and technical.  the crux of the route is at the beginning of the route.  make a difficult traverse left to gain a nice ledge and crack.  follow the crack to a funky groove.  get your groove on to a nice steep finish.  good varied climb that is worth the hike around.  this line dries fairly quick after a rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: retirement day: this overhanging route is full of pockets. finding the right combo makes for a fun ascent.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Coyote Cliff
text: golden box: fun over hung route 3 bolts up to ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Fire Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Front Porch Wall
text: de’lilah’s way: short crimps with a hug or two

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Front Porch Wall
text: waist of paper: funky little bulge midway.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Front Porch Wall
text: lying under the porch: pass a pocket to crimps and a jug or two.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Great Arch, The
text: dyn-o-mite: easy jug haul on beautiful holds, excellent length for new 5.9 leaders.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Great Arch, The
text: black powder: hop onto the ledge and stretch up to clip the bolt on the overhanging start. haul yourself over the initial overhang on good horizontals and thin plates, and then start angling out right and up. keep on truckin' through the continuous top half until you're at the anchors.  this line did feel a bit contrived to me. i had to constantly watch myself to make sure i wasn't climbing straight up into dyn-o-mite. but if you stay on route, the rock and the moves are nice. a worthwhile endeavor if you're looking for something a step up from dyn-o-mite.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Guide Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Guide Wall
text: mona lisa crack: starts up a crack

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Guide Wall
text: parks and rec: a tough start to crimps above.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Guide Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Indy Wall
text: face up to that arete: this short route begins as a slab and climbs the left side of the arete to an anchor below the roof.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Indy Wall
text: tight lipped: from the top of posse whipped follow a flake feature to a crimpy section to the anchors. great view!

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Indy Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Indy Wall
text: annie the annihilator: a must climb if you come to muir valley. located at the indy wall, this route is short but classic. a crimpy start leads to pumpy jug hauling up the slightly inverted face. the moves are just so cool and so fun, but suprisingly pumpy for such a short route.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Indy Wall
text: makin' bacon: start on the giant hueco/undercling to make a long, somewhat bouldery move. from here, an enduro-crimp fest awaits. short, and not all that pumpy unless crimps aren't your thing. one tricky move near the top to (you guessed it) a small crimp. awesome movement and cool holds. good technical skills will get you through this one just fine.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Inner Sanctum
text: netizen hacktivist: next bolted line past 'karmic retribution'.  climbs up a slab on shelves, edges, pinches and pockets.  elusive/deceptive start.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Inner Sanctum
text: bad company: just right of naughty neighbors 5.10d and from the same starting ledge... look for a nice flake about 10-15 feet up the route...  this was a nice warm up for some harder stuff... it suited as a warm up due to its nature of a few small holds then a good jug rest... a little sequntial but not wandery like the route to the left...

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Inner Sanctum
text: karmic retribution: very unique and aesthetic slab route. follows a black steak using ribs and interesting holds. interesting moves to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Inner Sanctum
text: naughty neighbors: a decent route on the left side of the first overhanging wall you get to at the inner sanctum area...  start by scrambling up on to the ledge from right to left then climb the crimpy head wall with a few good resting holds mixed in... the line wanders a little which i wasn't to crazy about but it is a good excercize in route finding... the crux comes at the end in the for of a few crimpy moves to gain the jugs at the top...

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: thanks holly: this climb is located on a definite arete.  you can climb to the right of the arete for a slabby experience, or on the arete itself.  the climb was a bit sandy/dirty as of oct. 2008, but still worth the while for a 5.8 leader.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: two chicken butts: a slabby route complete with a giant ledge just below the first bolt.  a little sandy/dirty as of oct 2008.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: 59" drillbitch: first line that that greets you when you get to johnnys wall. tricky first moves leads to good climbing on plates and some pockets. a little pumpy with a good dose of technical climbing in there for good measure. very fun route.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: bethel: just to the right of 59" and with similar character. interesting start leads to fun plate and pocket pulling, with a good finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: mancala: gain the ledge and continue on good 5.10 climbing to the crux lay back.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Johnny's Wall
text: spinner: similar to 59" and bethel, but with a more devious top section. good plates most of the way, with a top crimpy crux.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: prehistoric extermination: climb the short slabby start to pull through a reachy but short juggy plate section.  continue past the 6 bolts to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: coprolite: pocketed face with three bolts to chains. immediately right of basilisk.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: ryanosaurus: crimpy start to a small ledge, pull through a few more small pockets to get established above the bulge and then fire for the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: neanderfall: climb up the slab near the wide crack to a short overhanging pocketed section. climb the slopers to top out on the ledge with anchors. this route is almost always wet.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: watering hole: route is center (4th) of the 7 on this new wall. great reachy move over waist high roof. a nice first 5.10 lead.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Land Before Time Wall
text: sabertooth: tricky first couple of bolts. start directly under the first bolt, might wander a bit left. coming in from the ramp on the right takes all the fun out.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: shawty: the crux comes in reaching the chains. the is a really cool clipping open hand pinch to clip the chains.  this is the best of the three routes on this section of wall in my opinion.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: crescendo: the start is the toughest section.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: low exposure: easier start gains a thin crimpy section near the top. this route tops out and the anchors are located above the lip on a large boulder. if you follow the bolt lines directly it is harder than 5.8, the 5.8 climbs just right of the bolt line then shifts back left at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: mercenary of the mandarin chicken: this is the arete to the left of beta spewer, the route is different from everything to the left because it is overhung with big hold, a good introduction to rrg.  the crux comes between the second bolt and the anchors, just look for good holds the are there.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: crescent moon: bouldery start gains good moves to a solid reachy move past a blank section. depending on how you decide to move after the second bolt, the difficulty can vary!

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Practice Wall
text: beta spewer: climb okay holds up to a nice side pull/jug then get the next side pull.  get established and reach for a good crimp.  reach up high for a giant jug that looks like a horn. go left a bit on good holds then fire up to a decent hold then reach the anchors with big jugs again.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Recess Rock
text: hall monitor: short and bouldery vert route on the north face of recess rock, a fun little route to check out while the kids climb the slabs. avoid the temptation of stemming the tree if you don't want to downgrade it to 5.tree. can be set up on top rope by scrambling the backside of the boulder.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Shawnee Shelter
text: waterfall ballet: this is a fun romp up some steep jugs.  it looks more intimidating from the ground than it really is.  i would also say it is higher quality than the guide suggests, despite having a few dirty sections.  ape swing your way up some big flake and jug features until you reach the dubious iron oxide solution hole.  crux, figure out how to get past the solution hole and onto the flake feature above.  getting onto the flake is funky, but fun.  get a good stance for the last bolt, then move up the last flake and make a bit of a reach to get the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Slab City
text: thrillbillies: long moderate slab route up water grooved face.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: backstabber: pull a roof at the start and climb the face to the anchors hanging off the higher roof.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: where's my chisel: one move wonder stepping up onto the slab at the second bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: moonshine: start up a short section of rock with a single bolt protecting to reach a large ledge.  step right around the small arete and clip the next bolt.  the crux is getting through this short roof.  make some tough moves to get established above the next roof.  follow easier holds to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: sunbeam: climb the same start as moonshine.  stay left of the arete for a difficult roof pull.  clip the long ss cable hanging from the bolt and make very strenuous moves to get established above the roof.  follow pumpy slots and horizontals to the anchor.  beware the crux has ledge fall potential without a watchful belay.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: out of the dark: scramble up to the good first ledge, traverse out right, clipping the first bolt, and pull the roof. once you are on the ledge above the first roof, the second bolt is low, and the third bolt is easily reachable, making for an optional second bolt. (skipping the bolt does not seem to add any serious runout, but evaluate yourself.) the rest is decently pumpy, and clipping the anchors is not without some work.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunbeam Buttress
text: universal gravitation: desperate start followed by easy climbing to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunnyside
text: kokopeli's dream: crux is getting off the ground. a nice pitch on a face with holds on the arete to the left.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunnyside
text: virgin bolter tag team: begin by pulling past the obvious roof. rock and route quality drop after these opening moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunnyside
text: machete: begin with a sustained pocketed face up about 40 feet to an excellent rest. shake out and study the crux right above you, and when you're ready, pull the final roof to a large ledge with the anchors.  major style points if you actually mantle the last move instead of flopping onto your stomach.
feature_tags: crux, face, ledge, mantle, pocket, roof

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunnyside
text: dingo the gringo: this is a one-move wonder.  the crux is at the first bolt.  a stick clip is highly recommended due to the belay from a ledge and the move to get to the bolt.  start up a short overhang to a flared crack.  make a difficult move to get established in the crack.  then enjoy very easy slabbing to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Sunnyside
text: some humans ain't human: much better than its neighbor gringo.  start near the same ledge as gringo on the far right side of the wall.  a steep section leads a good rest and the first bolt.  make the big difficult move off the first bolt.  followed by a few more balancy technical moves.  trend back left slightly to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Tectonic Wall
text: tall cool one: fun route with good holds, just like the other three at tectonic.  pull through a big flake followed by a crack to a ledge.  climb your way to some massive ky plates after that to the easily clippable anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Tectonic Wall
text: plate tectonics: another classic...a tricky start leads to pumpy plate pulling pleasure...yeah!

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Tectonic Wall
text: gettin' lucky in kentucky: this climb is a classic "must-do" for the area...technical/pumpy climbing featuring pockets, jugs, and sidepulls with a steep finish.  enjoy!

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Tectonic Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Tectonic Wall
text: serpentine: the furthest left sport route on this section of wall, move left to a nice arete and balance your way to the chains on delicate feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: abby gabby goo: there is a hardish move getting off the ground to ok climbing. the route ends on a decent ledge, plenty of room for a couple people to stand on it. this makes it a good route to teach people to clean routes while being able to observe and double check their setup.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: hijacked project: a good warmup for the area but all-too-short.  tackle committing and fun moves through the initial roof and the first bolt. a stick-clip is recommended.  or, should you prefer to skip the roof, move in from the left on a ledge.   above the roof, follow big plates and good holds to a steep finish that comes all too soon. more rock looms above the anchors but...

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: one-armed bandit: this fun little route shares its opening moves with captain blondie before breaking right onto the arete and climbing the face above.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: stealing melinda: the crux is getting off the ground. pretty straight forward after that.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: cindarella: start in a shallow, right facing dihedral. boulder to the horizontal, then romp up the easy face above.   a stick clip is mandatory for this route- the '5.9' grade is what the book calls this route, but the start is hard 5.10- certainly as hard as armed insurrection.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: surfing the whale's back: clip the first bolt and climb up the chimney while reaching around the corner to clip the first few bolts. when the chimney seems unclimbable, swing around the arete and head up it. well protected, committing move at the end.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: armed insurrection: the rightmost route on the wall, starts at a very thin face, and moves up a fun looking wall above.   stick clip this one as well- the start is thin and the feet arent great.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Boneyard
text: tanduay time: the route has a couple longish moves to the first ledge. after the second ledge, head up a flake feature to some great sidepulling and under clings. last bolt to the anchors is a bit more run out than the rest of the route but it doesn't feel like it when you're up there.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: slabracadabra: start on the flake feature below the 3rd line of glue-in bolts. find the limonite knobs and delicately climb them using an occasional high step to an anchor in the overhang above. harder than it first appears, but good for honing footwork. a nice, but short intro to slab climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: yellow slabmarine: an interesting start leads to easier climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: africtionado: true friction climbing. unique for the red. smear your way up the nearly featureless slab right of slabracadbra trusting that your feet and climbing shoe rubber will match or exceed the coefficient of friction. some subtle mantle moves might be helpful.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: slabbatical: approximately 100 yards right of the main bowling alley routes. continue on the roadbed below the bowling alley for a couple of minutes until you see a pocketed boulder on your left. this small slabby cliff capped by a short overhang is immediately after and behind that boulder. this is the leftmost route on the slab wall. it has a reachy start and a couple of fun moves, but ends way too soon.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: imminent demise: pull on some pockets to start.  the first two moves are definitely the crux but if you find the right hand mono comfy it isn't too bad.  a big ledge follows this where you can get a major rest before tackling the slightly overhanging headwall.  there are many many choices for holds among all of the pockets but choose wisely because the majority of them are quite brittle

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: gaian prophecy: a small or medium piece of gear in the crack below the small alcove might be helpful getting to the high first bolt. climb good edges to the top. may be wet after a heavy rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Bowling Alley
text: ten pin: the crux is getting off the ground (may be easier for taller climbers or difficult for shorter climbers). long lock-offs on decent edges, but thin feet left of the first bolt is the easier start. a bouldery 5.11ish start on the slopey right facing left-leaning dihedral/flake feature to the right of the first bolt adds difficulty to the route. after the 1st bolt the climbing eases to 5.8 or 5.9 on good edges and pockets to a juggy ledge at the top.
feature_tags: crux, dihedral, flake, jug, ledge, pocket, sloper

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: ledgends of limonite: start as for glory and consequences, then trend left and up a fun arete to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: dynabolt gold: hardest moves are down low figuring out the start.  depending on height there are a couple different variations.  shorter people usually find it easier to start farther right on the overhang or jumping to the good hold just out of reach.  after clipping the first bolt it is more like 9+ all the way to the anchors. big holds and lots of rests if needed.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: bitter ray of sunshine: mantle start to a large ledge.  then huge jugs from there to a small roof with jugs to pull it on.  mantle start is the crux for sure

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: ledgends of limonite (direct start): the crux for the direct start is the first few moves under the large roof.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: touch of grey: tricky start up to a big ledge.  thin edges and big jugs to the top.  a couple of long moves but good clipping holds and stances.  crux is down low around the third bolt

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: muddy waters: thin vertical climbing on iron rails.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Great Wall
text: mingus: this climb starts in the same alcove as weapons of mass deception on the far left side of the great wall.  the first bolt is inside the alcove on the right hand wall. move right at bolt onto face.  the climb starts moderately and becomes progressively harder with an exciting but well protected step over move over the void below.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: international route of pancakes: the roofy start on this route is probably the hardest move (stick clip if you have any doubts).  the climbing eases up considerably after pulling the roof and makes a nice warmup.  continue up the arete to anchors at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: dance of the druids: slabby face right of the arching crack. big holds to grassy ledge, then up a thin but well-protected slab.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: moots madness: a tricky/reachy start leads to fun, easy climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: boltergeist: great climbing that never seems to quit.  soft for the grade, boltergeist makes a terrific choice for a leader's first 10b.  thin moves at the start make stick clipping a prudent choice.  climb on good edges and ledges past several bolts and a bulge to a nice rest ledge.  continue up the face to more purely slabby climbing at the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: beware the bear: moderate climbing on a pocketed and gently overhanging face. a little soft for the grade. the trick is finding the good handholds amongst thousands of not-so-good pockets. footholds abound.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: pre-emptive strike: pretty tough start.  don't go too far right or the climbing gets easier and not as fun.  pull the the really thin technical start to a technical slab.  climb through several bolts until you reach the steeper jug pulling section to the anchors.  fun line.  bottom felt a little harder than 10c to me but it was we and i had very little skin left on my fingers from two weeks of climbing

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: mantle peace: this very strange route is fun because it's so unique. climb onto a low protruding ledge and make awkward moves up the arete or slabby face to gain the next ledge. pull the crux roof and go right of the tree on the ledge. watch out for giant spiderwebs and an annoying prickly bush and move into the next steep section (crux #2). a final mantle puts you on top of the ledge at the chains.
feature_tags: arete, crux, face, ledge, mantle, roof, slab

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: cruisin' for a bruisin': a fun start leads to an interesting upper section.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Hideout
text: all mixed up: crux is getting through the crack

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Sanctuary
text: hot gossip: a long move off a formerly good chickenhead right off the ground is followed by two cool sequences involving heel hooks and a fat sloper. pull through some pockets to reach huge jugs then trend slightly right to a good stance. gain the slab and cruise to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: bg: climb the face until the holds fade, then reach around the arete for a blind side-pull. work the arete until the bolts stop just before some large blocks, then run it out on easy climbing to get on top of the ledge containing anchors for ed. clip one more bolt with an extended draw, if you wish, then make a few more moves to the chains above ed's anchor. bolted during bg's ("big gio's") first weekend back to climbing after a medical hiatus.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: ks: starts on the ledge above ed and bg. choose your own adventure: clip the bolts to climb as an extension of bg or plug some pro to climb as an extension of ed. primarily easier moves for the grade until a high crux pulling the bulge to get to the anchors. sport climbers will find the crux much easier if they ask their trad buddies how to hand jam first. the anchors look high from the ground, but a 60m rope is still plenty regardless of which route you're extending.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: scrumbulglazer: good, vertical route on nice gray stone.  starts with steeper climbing on juggy pockets and then ascends the less featured upper wall to a two bolt anchor.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: augenblick: vertical start leads to slightly easier climbing.  good climbing on edges, pockets, and smears.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: melancholy mechanics: good, vertical route on nice gray stone. starts with steeper climbing on juggy pockets and then ascends the less featured upper wall.  the route tends to meander right and left through the center section.  this route is still a little dirty, but should clean up nicely with more traffic.  the plaque at the base calls this route 5.11a, the guidebook calls it 5.10d.  it's a fine line, so you be the judge.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: treetop terror: climb past a finger crack flake to a slab above.  the route takes a mixture of gear and bolts.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > The Stadium
text: gnome wrecker: interesting slab and face climbing just right of black tide before you get to the pessimist. an awkward anchor placement at the top detracts somewhat.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Washboard Wall
text: heard it on npr: this long route is the left-most sport route on the washboard wall. locate the high first bolt left of "spider crux". you may want to place a piece of pro here. follow five bolts up moderate terrain to a spacious ledge with a two-bolt anchor. belay here to reduce rope drag or continue through the overhanging pocketed face past six more bolts to another two-bolt anchor. use a 60m rope.  i strongly suggest belaying from the intermediate anchors for the top part. the rope drag up top is horrendous when your belayer is at the bottom.

location: Red River Gorge > Muir Valley > Washboard Wall
text: barenjager: big moves good holds

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Emerald City
text: whiteout direct (aka nerds): climb easy, but off balance moves to a distinct crux where the angle changes from vertical to low angle. the climbing is much easier after the crux.   one first time climber, having trouble with the crux moves was reported to have called out, "these nerds are hard to hang on to!"  check out the cool iron oxide features.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Emerald City
text: diamond in the rough: an excellent sport route up thin, crimpy holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Emerald City
text: ruby slippers: another great climb on emerald city.  a great circuit for this area is to access the ledge and do all 5 adjacent climbs without untying your shoes or rope.  just right of the obvious scoop at the bottom of flying monkeys lies another bolted line. climb up the edge of the "dish" and head for anchors at the top. there may be no particular crux on this climb, but it is not without some hard moves. the holds are small, but mostly good. wear your edging shoes!

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Global Village
text: kentucky pinstripe: this is a tricky route down low. boulder up and establish yourself on the face. then delicately balance your way to the arete. relax to the ledge. rest, take in the view and then launch up the upper face.   the upper face has the best position of any route of this grade in the rrg.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Global Village
text: loosen up: a fun route. however, be ready. moderately overhung with generous holds, it lulls many into thinking it's a typical rrg jughaul...only to be spanked near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Global Village
text: dog fight (a.k.a. circa man): fun slab climbing to a crux roof to some more fun slab.  tough on the finger skin but worth the effort if your in the area.  the clips aren't as spread out as the guide makes it seem.  climb up the iron oxide crimpers, slopers, and side pulls to get below the roof for a decent rest.  make the tough technical moves over the roof to get to the good hold just past some cool knobs.  gain the ledge below the last bolt.  make a few more difficult strechy moves to gain the anchors.
feature_tags: crimp, crux, ledge, roof, slab, sloper, technical

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: all cows eat grass: climb the nice edgey slab to a bulge. pull around some goofiness and finish in a weird groove, making an airy move or two right or alternately finish on thin holds from directly under the anchor. either way, the finish is the metal crux of the route.  good climbing that flows well up to the second bolt from the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: valor over discretion: starts from the top of a large boulder.  climb the face right of an arete to a roof, then move to the left face and finish at a ledge.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: trouble clef: arrive early. like many climbs at roadside crag, this is a well used route. this route starts to the right of a crack, and on top of a waist high ledge. take a minute to enjoy the view from the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: jump for joy: start on top of a boulder at the base of the rock and pull on to the face- clipping 4 bolts along the way to a long ledge with trees and a bolted anchor for a belay/rap. this route is probably harder for shorter people, but not obscenely so.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: kampsight: similar in nature to c sharp or b flat, but harder. there is a couple of distinct cruxes at 1/3 and 2/3 height. the route is intimidating if you are breaking into the grade.   the moves are very fun once you get comfortable on this route and the exposure at the top is good.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: altered scale: stiff for the grade, altered scale has a nice variety of moves.  starting on a ledge, pull some hard moves to the first bolt (stick clipping is a good option).  continue on easier ground to a thin section about midway; save some energy for pulling a sequency bulge near the top, then finish to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: fadda: face climb the bolt line on mostly pockets through a high crux to cold shuts.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: a.w.o.l: brilliant stone, great moves and your belayer will be blocking the  trail, so anyone who wanders up to the wall will be forced to watch you climb this route.  awol is one of the best known routes at the grade in the rrg.   this was my first 5.10 redpoint and i had been terribly intimidated by the finishing moves for a long time. it was very tricky to find my way through all the chalked up crimps while pumped silly.  but then one night i had a dream where i flowed effortlessly through the final sequence and i sent the route the next day.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: hard left: climb up the slab to gain a left-angling crack that eventually ends.  from here, traverse left to a large hueco and a two bolt anchor.

route: You Can Tune a Piano, but You Can't Tuna Fish
location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: you can tune a piano, but you can't tuna fish: challenging face climbing with a short crux section about midway.  starting on a slabby section, balance your way to the first bolt about 15' up.  work through crimpy features up to a slightly overhanging crux; good footwork will put you in a position to throw for a nice jug.  continue up the face to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: crazyfingers: a steep climb with mostly good holds, but little good rest. none of the moves are particularly hard, but the route is pumpy, making the clips up top harder than the other two routes, but perhaps this is the best warm-up,  for lack of hard moves down low.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: dragonslayer: a short pitch, but the whole thing is good. the brevity of it is mitigated by the chance to climb it, awol, and crazy fingers all back-to-back, for 150 feet of great climbing, all at ~ the same grade and character.just a few feet right of a.w.o.l. is a second climb of a similar grade, perhaps a shave harder. your success on this climb is dependent on having some finger strength, and on finding and using some thin footholds. the monos are not 'hangers' because you have good feet to hold your weight, they are just for holding you in, so the stress is not incredible. the route also gets easier as you progress.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: pulling pockets: the fourth route on the 5.10 wall, between crazyfingers (5.10c) and the trad line synchronicity (5.11a).  originally a trad line, this excellent route is now well protected by bolts.  climb through pockets to a crimp crux, then pick one of several variations from the last bolt to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
region_2: Graining Fork Nature Preserve (a.k.a. Roadside Crag)
text: just duet: great balancy climbing the whole way

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > Bird Cage Sector (CLOSED)
text: gunner: climb easy climbing up fun slab moves to a shut down crimpy crux right before the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > Bird Cage Sector (CLOSED)
text: botanical gardens: make a burly move off some cheater stones to mantel on to a ledge. move right up big holds make your way on to the slab and climb slab for what seems forever to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > Bird Cage Sector (CLOSED)
text: dirty bird: climb the bolted arete on the far right side of the crag. start with bouldery moves to a rest then more bouldery moves to a rest and then finally climb out some giant jugs over a bulge on to the slaby finish to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > Bird Cage Sector (CLOSED)
text: here comes the beep beep: fun and techy line that requires balance and a calm head.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > Bird Cage Sector (CLOSED)
text: lone coyote: less than vertical climb with a tough boulder move near the bottom and a spicy move to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > The Old Zoo (CLOSED)
text: put me in the zoo: a good route by it's own merit, but popular mostly as a warm up for the rest of the lines at the zoo.  the route is on small holds on a near vertical wall, but only has a few moves at the grade down low.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > The Old Zoo (CLOSED)
text: chimp: another good route on the smoother side of the wall, but has a few steep moves on a roof and bulges. as such, it is a mix of crimps and larger holds, still with a balance of crimps. pocket fans can skip this one as well.  if "put me in the zoo (9+)" is occupied, the might be the best warm up for you.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > The Old Zoo (CLOSED)
text: one brick shy: this climb is a mix of characters typical of the left and right sides of the wall. the bottom has the pockets and steepness expected to the left, and the top the slabby crimps expected on the climbs located on the right side of the wall... and somewhere in between is somewhere in between.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > The Old Zoo (CLOSED)
text: armadillo: another route for the folks who prefer edges and ledges to pockets, but still a route requiring strength. long lock-offs are the key to the climb and shorter climbers might find it more difficult, perhaps the reason for its early 5.11a rating.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > The Zoo (CLOSED) > The Old Zoo (CLOSED)
text: jailbird: another blank looking cripy crux leading to better holds... this one isn't quite as stiff as edgehog 5.10d but isnt as interesting either...  climb the blank looking slab over some super tiny holds to better holds and easier climbing... the only challenge other than the slab is a pull over a short roof that isn't too diufficult at all compaired to the start... after the roof cruise to the top, aint nothing stoppin you...  the only negative thing about this route was that it seemed dirty, more so than the others in the area...

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: dream of a bee: 5.8 pocket pulling to the right of wadcutter.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: cordelia: slabby, with all that means. crux is between the 3rd and 4th bolts

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: tourist trap: this fun and engaging route climbs up through a funky start to reach the obvious arete above. climb this to the anchors.  a stick clip is advised as the start is not a give-away.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: wadcutter aka "gumby killer": a pinchy vertical line with few rests. straight up the slightly overhanging wall using crimpers and plenty of edging. climb right of the overhang to finger pockets, then up to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: rest assured: on the left side of the 5.10 wall, climb an obvious crack/corner to a small roof.  pull it and angle right and up the face above.  the start is shared with family values (5.10c).

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: reanimator: a fun route with a burly start. a stick clip is a good idea.   climb up through a burly start on good holds to a traverse out to the wall above. once on the wall, take the left hand line to the anchors above.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: family values: on the left side of the 5.10 wall, climb an obvious crack/corner to a small roof.  pull it and angle left and up the face above to an obvious crux at mid-height, then continue up easier ground to the top.  the start is shared with rest assured (5.10a).

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: poopie head: 5.10 can be very steep at the red river gorge. poopie head is a fine example. if only it were longer!   climb up small but good pockets to the high first bolt. a clip stick could prove useful here. continue up to the second bolt and to a small roof. pull up over it and hang on to bigger holds on steepening terrain to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: stool sample: overall, the holds on this are worse than poopie head, but the crux on stool sample is easier.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: last resort: either clip the bolt on the front face that is entirely covered in moss and climb through vegetation, or start on the logical first bolt of family values and step left at the ledge. climb mossy rock off the ledge through a thin section up to a juggy, sideways flake in a bulge. figure out where the next holds are and pull over, then continue up worsening rock to the top. fairly run-out in many spots.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: spock's pockets: find the path of least resistance up the right side of the arête and continue up the featured wall above. the features unfortunately do not make the most ideal or intuitive climbing holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: pork and bondage: play "guess the pocket" as you near a low bulge. pull over it to easier territory before pulling over another bulge to a shake before the steep runs to the anchors on mostly jugs.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: it's alive: shares a start with reanimator. begin with or without some cheater stones to grab the first jugs under the low roof. pull the roof, traverse out left to gain a stance, and then move right to follow the line of bolts to some anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Natural Bridge Region > Torrent Falls (Limited Access)
text: pocket pussy: cool pocketed face to a slight bulge, trending left towards anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Camp Store Crag
text: store: solid route for the grade. start up near the arete, and climb pockets and crimps to a small overhang, pull the overhang and continue up the face to the right. don't think it's over until you reach the top!

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Eastern Sky Bridge Ridge
text: drop the anchor: nothing remarkable about this route other than that it is one of the very few easy sport routes in the area.  climb a line of big holds near the bolts to a small roof and then up to the anchors. watch out for drag- and rap instead of lower off to save wear on your rope.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Eastern Sky Bridge Ridge
text: jack in the pulpit: by virtue of its grade, it has always been *the* warm up at the area.  mostly good holds on a slightly steep wall. the crux is probably just an endurance problem for most climbers, so it's a good one to "go for it" on.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Funk Rock City
text: manic impression: a little ways past cruising lane and rite of passage is a broad, tall well featured slab. this is the left of the two bolted routes. the crux is going for the anchors and requires jedi mind control and precision footwork. the route up to the crux is pretty casual at 5.7-8 or so. a must do if you're in the area. one of the best 5.10a sport routes in the rrg.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Funk Rock City
text: funkadelic: this is the right of the two lines on the big slab at funk rock. you may want a medium sized cam up high to protect a long runout. the crux is somewhat height dependant and bouldery, and the rest of the climb is more moderate. very fun moves and very cool rock. the finishing moves to the anchors are very delicate and you should take care as there is a ledge you can hit. it's happened before.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Funk Rock City
text: red hot chilli pepper: a rarity in the red, being a climb with a low angle crux, with small holds. climb up pockets and horizontals past a few bolts and gear placements (small-med cams or tricams) and get into the business, a low angled slab with small holds.  continue to the shuts and rap off.  lowering off and tr-ing are less advisable on this route, since the angle of the rock seems to create a twist in the rope as it goes.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Left Flank
text: face up to that crack: follow the bolt line through a short, nice handcrack then more bolts to chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Left Flank
text: mr. bungle: this fun route ascends a blunt arete.  start just left of the arete, move up and right to the arete, then up to chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Left Flank
text: brother stair: a short climb, but some interesting climbing...  just around the corner right from the approach trail to left flank, there is a short climb on some steep rock.  climb up off-angle pockets for the crux of this one past a total of four bolts to the anchor.  i believe this climb was named after a local preacher in the early 90's.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Left Flank
text: fast food christians: a bouldery, reachy crux leads to much easier climbing above.

route: To Defy the Laws of Tradition
location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Left Flank
text: to defy the laws of tradition: a great pocketed route with lots of chalk up a slightly overhanging face.  the technical crux is down low; the enduro crux is up high.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Long Wall
text: rock caddie: face route climbs good holds. probably not worth the long hike but worth it if you've come over to do gladuator

route: Boom! Boom! Out Go the Lights
location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Long Wall
text: boom! boom! out go the lights: a strange route with a strange name. despite not following a particular or natural line,  the climb is still good mileage and fun.  climb up a bulging start where a little power is helpful, going up to an easier face and then right to an arete, then to a good ledge with a bolted anchor. a bit of a strange route.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Long Wall
text: back door to paris: this climb is ok and worth doing if you are waiting to get on another line. it follows jugs and crips to a small roof where the anchors are.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: mercy miss percy: somewhere between ok and just bad...  it depends on how wet it has been lately and if anyone has recently climbed it. or perhaps it has cleaned up with time?  if not, then climb up past a line of bolts on increasingly dirty rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: sunshine: a short moderate sport climb that has always held the masses at military, being one of few 'soft' warm-ups at the cliff.  the crux of this, the center of the 3 bolted lines in this short section is not so much any individual move, but the pump associated with finishing the route.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: moonbeam: this is the left-most of three closely spaced routes on the short steep section of rock. a distinct steep crux down low on dark edges and pockets is the business while the upper section lets off on the difficulty. still, the climb is pumpy enough to warm you up for harder climbs.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: stay left: an ok route on ok rock. nothing wrong with it, but not a destination climb. i felt like it "didn't flow" for whatever that is worth. climb past 4 bolts on the face (without moving out right to the chimney?) to the anchors. not terribly great, but not bad.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: danita dolores: the base of this route has changed over it's history, prompting some differences in opinion about the difficulty of the route, which has waxed and waned over time.  in 1991 when the route was bolted, a large tree stood not far from its base. one could stand there, reach up to a hold and hop to a second hand and pull up onto the route. this was the crux and was about middle 5.10. shorter and less powerful climbers complained about the sandbag.  in perhaps 1994 a huge windstorm and some tornadoes came though the gorge in autumn, blowing many trees across roads and trails. the tree at the base of d.d. was just one more casualty, but it made the route easier...  the root system tore out and brought soil and rocks up, and placed a starting shelf at the base of the climb.  one could simply step off of these and onto the climb, making any sort of hop-start seem contrived and unnecessary.  some people complained that the route was over graded.  over time, earth settled, the tree collapsed, rocks were moved and low and behold, the start to this climb has returned, perhaps to a lower point than before?  and now i note the latest guidebook mentions a "desperate start" again.  so whatever the condition, do what is necessary to pull up onto the wall over the bulging start, and climb easier, lower-angle rock to the top of the arete out right and rap from fixed anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: in the light: this is the right-most of the 3 "triplet" routes on the short wall just left of the main approach to military. the route was bolted much later than the first two on this wall but perhaps should have gone in sooner, as it is it is a good addition to the cliff. this climb is slightly longer and slightly harder than the other two routes nearby, and is a logical line that mitigates the crowd waiting on the other two warm-up lines. i may also be a better project for the moderate sport leader.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Military Wall
text: possum lips: the crux of this climb depends upon your strengths and may have changed over time. the small holds were getting smaller in the mid 1990's and i suspect may have continued to do so.   this route was named after a semi-local climber at the time and who might not have been so well liked by the fa party (?). i don't know the complete story and never asked.  climb up a low angle slab with small and sloping holds to reach the anchor, all the while admiring the big pockets to your left on fuzzy undercling.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pebble Beach
text: scabies: climb the bolted flake between two moderate cracks for 40' to shuts at the top.  a nice change of pace from most sport climbs at the red.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pebble Beach
text: blood money: this route climbs up orange rock through a couple of roofs with a hard move near the first bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pebble Beach
text: reserved seating: a great route with a great rest straddling the arete that earned this unique route its name.  climb up good rock and good holds until you are just starting to feel a pump, then take a seat and shake out. consider it a good thing that it is reserved, there is only room for one here... then once shook out, finish past a few more bolts to the anchor.  a pretty good lead for beginning leaders.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pebble Beach
text: ju ju: another good low-angle line on good rock. if you are sick of pulling on pockets and want to edge a little, and have already climbed out the emerald city area, try this climb and its neighbors. work your way up the right side of the blunt, low-angle arete to the top, below the huge roof of the "trash compactor" rockhouse to a bolted anchor shared with sundance. (the next bolted line to the right).

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pebble Beach
text: sundance: start up a few moves in the offwidth and traverse right on good holds to below the initial bolt, then climb up on thin holds on a low angle face along a line of bolts. this is generally a body-length right of the offwidth crack.  where the crack ends, trend left up above it to the bolted anchor, which is shared with juju, the arete to the left.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: lord of the flies: head up the heavily pocketed face, also utilizing the arete on the left when necessary.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: creature feature: a "hero" climb with one cool steep move and a lot of huge holds.get up to the ledge at the base of the route, just below the big roof and clip a bolt. lean out over the roof to some big holds and ape your way onto those. you can practically campus the route from there, but heel-hooks look cooler. clip a bolt above the roof and pull up to stand on the less-than-vertical face. continue up on plates and puzzle pieces to a set of anchors and lower off. a rarely done extension continues on plates and edges to the top of the cliff face with nuts and slings for gear.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: pogue ethics: a long route on jugs and plates. the crux comes about halfway up, when you are forced to negotiate a bulge. there is a sit-down ledge rest before the crux, though.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: perverse intentions: start on a hill, just left of a large flake/chimney there are a series of right and wrong open hand moves up and left.  clipping holds are all good so find the right ones.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: overlord: technical, balancey, slabby route.  very atypical of the red river gorge.  lots of small crimps up the face, with the crux coming near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Phantasia
text: creep show: a pumpy 10d next to a technical 11b.  i've heard it several times that climbers believed that the grades on these two routes were reversed!  get on to the left of the two sport routes and head up and left on it into an awkward and pumpy left-leaning flake. balance and grip your way to the anchors on this climb, then compare to the route to the right...

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pistol Ridge
text: danger mouse: start on a big jugg pocket and stand up onto the wall.  taller people can reach the next good hold from here.  shorter people may have to step the feet up higher to get the right hand.  clip the first bolt from here. climb up and right towards the massive under clings.  easy pockets until clipping the last bolt.  short bit of barren face is probably the crux.  high feet and stand up to major jug just below the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pistol Ridge
