text: it's a wonderful life: good climbing for a 9.  this is  a really fun route and the view is amazing.  the crux comes just after clipping the third bolt.  another hard section to clip the second bolt above the huge rest ledge.  can be done in two pitches to reduce rope drag.  climb to giant rest ledge, belay the second up, then climb the second pitch.   usually done in one pitch though.    can top out to a second set of anchors also.  it is a bit run out from the firs set to the second set and the climbing doesn't ease up much.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Pistol Ridge
text: chem studs: boulder past the first bolt to easier ground. lower from anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Purple Valley
text: captain one eye: starting near a tree growing at the base of the cliff, climb up and right on plates and chicken-heads past several bolts to reach good horizontals on lower angled rock. on an early ascent of this climb on a cold morning i jammed my hand back into a horizontal and reached down o my harness for a piece of gear to place into it. i was surprised to feel something smooth and slick jammed in the very back of the crack and much more surprised still when that smooth slick something started moving under the force of my jam. i ran quickly from that spot. my partner climbed carefully around it, peeking in and reporting to me that i was lucky not to have been bitten by a now very awake copperhead!  perhaps the cold morning made it less aggressive or perhaps i'd accidentally pinned down its head.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Purple Valley
text: come in your lycra: climb pockets and ledges through 4 bolts to the chain anchors.  the chains can be reachy if you clip them low on the climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Purple Valley
text: 5.11 jimmy and spike go craggin': climb the face/arete past 2 bolts to reach a small horizontal below the overhang.  place a piece here and climb over the bulge on good holds to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Purple Valley

location: Red River Gorge > Northern Gorge > Wall of Denial
text: toxic avenger: i don't like to call this route a sport route. it's a bolted route for sure, but there are only 4 bolts in 60 feet and no separate anchors for this one.   to some it will seem runout and to others the bolts will seem undersized.   regardless, this is a classic route and deserves your attention.  edge up a black streak to the ledge. traverse left until you can move up on to the ledge and belay from anchors above buckeye testpiece.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bob Marley
text: seeds n stems: begin by getting onto two ledges, then enjoy a plethora of pocket jugs all the way to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bob Marley
text: waiting for jj: pull a small bulge on jugs and continue up the juggy face to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bob Marley
text: where's jj?: pull the roof on huge jugs then balance your way up pockets of a variety of shapes and sizes.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bob Marley
text: the ultimate crumbsnatch: if your arms are shot from all the cave climbing, come take on this novel rrg leg pumper, tucked away in one of the best, bob marley approved chill spots. pull through the start, where holds actually exists, then take on the impossible face by stemming and chimneying your way to the lip. keep your head together after clipping the last bolt, as the 5.3 run to the anchor is a definite no fall zone (the pg13 section).clean with caution!use the 1st draw to lower through, and collect it with a stick clip once you're safely back on the ground, or stay clipped into the belayer's side to keep you from swinging over too fast after retrieving the first draw.

route: 5.10 Until Lee and Jeff Do It
location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: 5.10 until lee and jeff do it: amazing, slightly steep, easy route with the best holds i've ever felt. be gentle with a few though, as they may not hold forever. definitely the best warmup on the wall. this is a must do just for that warm fuzzy feeling you get when climbing on never ending jugs.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: spyder's hangout: climb up large pockets and jugs on this short route. easy climbing, but ledge fall potential at the second bolt. warm up on the easier, slightly steeper 5.9+ with better holds just right of this line.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: my mind escapes me: techy slab! believe!!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: upworthy: starts by jumping/pulling up on an obvious two-handed jug (harder), or by climbing up easier (and chossier) terrain on the left and traversing right. either way gets you to the wide ledge at the bottom of a large scoop, and the route moves up and right from there.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: muffintop: mostly big jugs with a tricky move or two, this route is a nice warmup for the wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Bronaugh Wall
text: fever pitch: techy, somewhat mossy slab with very good movement.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: brolo el cunado: start on some side-pulls then it eases up with jugs and pockets. fun!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: tiger lily: creep up the low angle slab until you can grab the flake above the second bolt and pull up to the finish

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: my way or the highway: follow bolts through a series of bulges with a nice slab guarding the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: [redacted]: this route is the best warm up around.  start on smaller holds and reach to better jugs as you go up.  interesting movements, and the holds only get larger as you climb.  well protected.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: raindancer: a tricky no feet start leads to a heavily pocketed face and easier climbing above.  short route and a good warm-up.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: brown eyed girl: climbs a less than vertical slab via a series of edges and horizontals.  good warm-up route.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: motor booty pimp affair: adventure climb to the fullest! this route has a touch of everything you normally don't get in the red. slabby start lower quality rock, gives way to bulges, crimps, low angle stemming and a brief lie back. take in all 95' of this engaging climb. crux section lets you choose to pull crimps on a bulge or stem up a sandy low angle gully. a 60m will get you down, but tie a knot if lowering.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: good gravy: i thought this was a fun climb, but a bit stiffer than the guide book's rating of 10b. the moves to the first bolt are fun and lead to a crux between the second and third bolt. this route didn't seem to get a lot of traffic and the route was covered in a lot of lichen and spider webs, but with traffic should be a lot more enjoyable.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: when rats attack: bolted line that climbs up an arete through a couple bulges.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: baby blue eyes: similar to its neighbor, "brown eyed girl", this route climbs the less than vertical slab using a series of edges and horizontals.  just a little less featured.  pretty good route.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: that's what she said: follow the bolts up the easier technical slab. a good warm up for the 11s on this section of wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: flying the bird: slabby climbing, make sure your manteling is up to par.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Chica Bonita Wall
text: old english: move up ledgy rock for the first few bolts to reach the huge flake feature. lay-back the very overhung flake feature on huge jugs to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Courtesy Wall
text: std: climb large iron oxide jugs below to a crimpy and reachy crux. small but good intermediates exist for shorter climbers at the crux if you look for them.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Courtesy Wall
text: buenos hermanos: climb iron rails past a short flake feature in the middle of the wall. from the large jug shelf, bear down through extremely thin crimps, technical feet, and a pair of garbage slopers.expect a lot of dirt and lichen, although it would actually climb quite well if cleaned up.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: sudoku: pull through a boulder problem and then continue on jugs to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: waltz the deal: climb some low angle slab up to the roof. clip bolt and continue onto some interesting climbing.  or, do the direct start going straight (left of the slab). goes at about the same grade.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: single finger salute: just to the left and around the corner from ghost in the machine, single finger salute is better than its neighbor to the right, second labor of hercules. cruxy off the ground to a no hands rest, climb the roof on good jugs, then establish out of the roof on smaller holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: action over apathy: climb crimpy pockets to a small roof pull the roof straight over (don't cheat left) and then follow pockets to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: curbside no traction: surprisingly fun slab route with a flake thrown in about halfway up for good measure. can be dirty after it rains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: the second labor of hercules: tough face climbing to a good no hands rest then there's a short over-hanging sprint to the last bolt and anchors

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Curbside
text: ghost in the machine: this route makes a nice warm up for the other lines on this wall.   start just to the right of the arete and climb straight up using very positive holds to reach a large ledge at mid height.   pulling the moves off this large ledge is the crux.   once established above the ledge, it's jugs to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: pottsville escarpment: a long, pleasent slab pitch that follows good edges and flaring cracks.  the start and the middle are the steepest and hardest part of the route.  the first 6 feet is a bit grungy, but once on the route the rock is great.  definitely want a stick clip.  this is an excellent option for when the 5.10's at the main drive-by crag are mobbed.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: layback and groove: lie back the difficult crack\corner, then move left onto the steep face and up into the headwall to stellar finish on giant "chicken head" flakes!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: deeper is better: to the right of whip stocking is this fun juggy line. gain the ledge using large jugs then continue up the interesting arete feature before continuing up on sharp edges and jugs to a hole with anchors in it.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: make  a wish: this route has good holds but odd sequences. used as the area warmup but nowhere near as fun as the rest.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: slick and the 9mm: this route climbs better than you think it will.  make some pretty easy moves to a good rest and climb through the bulge (crux) quickly.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: harshin' my mellow: slightly overhanging with good holds for most of the way.  do some easy climbing to the base of a short corner.  a few stemming moves brings you to the base of the steeper headwall.  a brief crux on slopey edges gain better holds.  look for the cool knob hold and enjoy a quick hand crack just below the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: a wave new world: the route start is 10' left of make a wish. climb interesting move up the corner past two bolts, clip the 3rd bolt, (find the no hands knee bar rest and clipping stance) decipher the tricky technical crux which leads to the horizontal ledge. traverse left past a bolt and then climb straight up to gain the opposing shallow cracks\side pulls, (better on the left). climb up the face past two more bolts to the anchor. you can climb out right to a large pocket for a better stance to clip the anchor.
feature_tags: crack, crux, face, ledge, pocket, technical

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: breakfast burrito: fun plate climbing leads up to a very large ledge. rest and get ready for the steep exciting finish. pull around the arete and follow great holds to the top!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: fire and brimstone: good holds lead to a crimpy crux about mid way up. after this you get a decent rest and power past a big sloper to the top. really fun climbing on great holds!!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: sojourner truth: easy jugs plates to a scoop below a steeper upper half.  negotiate a wandering sequence of edges and pockets to reach the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Drive-By Crag
text: the midnight gospel: take on the left or right start, then find your way to a cruxy big move through the blank panel at the 4th bolt where you'll be faced with another interesting decision. dont let up after this, as there are still some real moves left to tick this one off!sun until 130ishstays dry in heavy rain

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Far Side
text: on watch in the notch: hard but good start, then pockets and side pulls to the finish. angles slightly right at the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Far Side
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Far Side
text: snow day: start by stemming between the detached boulder and the wall. decide when to leave the comfort of the ledge and commit to the face. climb on pockets and edges to the anchor. as of early 2021, this route has a good bit of lichen / dirt on it - bring a brush.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Far Side
text: subject to change: this route is reached by heading right from the notch and making your way along the base of the cliffline (not up the steep hill, nor down the road).  crimpy moves with a few underclings - finesse your way to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Far Side
text: nameless: climb underclings and slopers past several tough moves that do not really let up.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Left Field
text: jet lag: climb a fat flake leading to a small bulge. pull the bulge and continue on big ledges to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Left Field
text: thru space and time: balance moves start this climb up to a small roof about 10 feet from the ground, then lead to a crimpy, edgy, technical face to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Left Field
text: apoplectic chick from missouri: climb through and overhanging section to a blank face. negotiate the blank section, then continue on larger holds to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > North 40
text: ticket redemption: past the two cracks is a bolted arête. pull over the undercut start, then follow comfortable slots, sidepulls, & pockets as you move back and forth up the corner.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Purgatory
text: the gimp: make a few quick pulls to get off the ground and into more interesting balance moves.  then continue up the steepening face on decent holds.  fight the pump (if this isn't just a warm-up for the more difficult popular lines here).

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Purgatory
text: jumbo shrimp: starts with a bit of slab climbing that quickly gets steeper; then pull a small overhang on holds appropriate for the grade.  slightly harder than that route to it's left.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: NA

text: days of thunder: sorta fun if the other routes are occupied.  a little dirty with an interesting stem move or supposedly crux sloper sequence higher up

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: monobrow: fun route, good variety of moves, interesting arete climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: delayed gratification: this face climbs like something out of the gym.  start at a right facing flake.  make a couple of technical moves to get above onto the big iron horizontals.  make a long move to gain a thin horizontal (crux) near the beginning of the face section.  then follow huge iron ledges to a short section of pockets to the top fighting the pump the whole way.
feature_tags: crux, face, flake, ledge, pocket, technical

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: hatfield: this route has cleaned up very nicely leaving some beautiful pockets and edges up a slightly overhanging technical face.  definitely an area classic.  begin up the easy slab for a few bolts.  start up the steepening face.  make moves between thin edges, pockets, and an occasional jug.  fight the pump the entire way to the anchors.  this climb has a lot less shake outs than its neighbor so keep moving.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: mccoy: start in the awkward layback to good holds. follow the good holds to a dirty ledge. pull the weird roof thing anyway you can and then follow much easier moves up the vertical face to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Rival Wall
text: ultimate rival: start left of a small dihedral and climb past 4 bolts to a no-hands rest at a break in the cliff. clip the 5th bolt and pull the roof using crimps, pockets, and a decent right foot hidden in some manky looking rock.  clip the 6th bolt after pulling onto the roof and keep it together on decent edges and pockets to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Shady Grove
text: listerine girl: climb to a dish then move out onto a tongue feature before hitting the roof. finish on well-featured slab before chains

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Shady Grove
text: street fight: fun slab with a short but very footsy crux at the 3rd bolt.  make a few crimp moves and pull into a large scoop.  move right and engage the techy crux which relies more on footwork than finger strength.  the last 40 feet is much easier.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Shady Grove
text: girls gone wild..woo!: 2nd leftmost route on the wall. a classic jug haul up an aesthetic line

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Solar Collector/Gold Coast

text: super pinch: this pockety route has many choices of holds and pretty much all of them are sharp. the iron rock edges are not just at the lips but there are additional edges inside the pockets. that said you don't have to hold on that hard since the holds will grab your skin for you.  long pulls between relatively good hold, though the next ne always seems just a bit further than it should be. quite continuous for the grade and you never really get two good holds side by side or a good hold to match and rest on.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Bright Side
text: crazy eyes: short and rather chossy climb with a small roof in the middle.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Bright Side
text: pickpocket: hard start on painful rock to easier climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: deeznuts: climb just right of a crack using face holds and and the crack to make it to a bulging feature just before the anchors.  this route can be climbed on gear.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: spoiler bait: climb good ledges to fun slab moves. finish on a monster bucket

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: boilerplate: super fun climbing for the grade with everything from slab to slightly overhung. heady, exposed feeling at the top (crux section)!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: love potion  9: fun face climbing for the first half of the route, and sloping slots with tricky feet for the second half

route: Sitting on Top of the World
location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: sitting on top of the world: mostly vertical with a couple of bulges. slab finish

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: just goosin’: a heavily featured vertical face with a couple of bulges that angles up right through a slab section to a ledge, then up a right side bulge past a roof to the anchors. there is a link with a biner on the second to last bolt to make cleaning and pulling the rope easier. leave it so your rope won’t get stuck on the pine tree to right.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: lightly salted: slab with some spice in the middle. trust your feet.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: the pressure principle: solid slab climbing on solid rock.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: a1a: left-most bolted route on the face with the wave shaped roof. crux is down low. nice rock with fun moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: banjolero: a fun steep and pocketed route that saves the crux for the last move.  start in a dihedral feature where left wall is covered in pockets.  make the easy moves to get to the first bolts.  get into the dihedral feature using and use the steep pockets to get through the next few bolts.  move left at the top onto a flake feature on the left face.  hurry up and make the last few tough moves before your arms give out and clip the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: fairweather friend: a varied line that throws a little slab, stemming and pump at you.  awkward pods and pockets on a slab lead to a mantle off some classically southern slopers.  follow an easy corner with pockets in the crack until the angle steepens.  a brief stemming crux on scoops gains nice pockets to the top.
feature_tags: crack, crux, mantle, pocket, slab, sloper

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: n4: forty feet of fun with a nice solid crux at the third clip

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Crossroads
text: yell fire!: a good slab problem that requires good footwork and some confidence.  start at the left end of the wave like roof.  slap and smear your way to the first stance on the short flake feature.  make thin moves up to the next bolt below the roof.  figure out how to make the tough stand up to shoot for the jug at the roof.  make a few more difficult moves to get above the roof and enjoy the easier slab to the last section of pockets.  pull through moderate pockets on some steep terrain to get to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Dark Side
text: small fry: a fun little route to pass the time if you're waiting in line on the main wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Dark Side
text: padawan: padowan is a good moderate that climbs vertical stone on heavily featured pockets and plates.  begin with some steep moves to gain the wall, heading up and right.  the route eases as you ascend, with a bit of difficulty coming right before the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Dark Side
text: younglings: climb the clean face on consistent edges and a variety of pockets to a set of cruxy crimps up top. might serve as a slightly better warm up for the fingers than its juggier neighbors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Dark Side
text: barn dance: this neglected slab follows some interesting features, and offers some fun knob pulling.  stick clip the first bolt, then do some delicate moves to reach a right-trending crack.  hug past a protruding column, navigate through some large knobs, and then mantle into a large, slopey hueco.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: 27 years of climbing: great spicy climb for the beginning leader. huge holds with great movements

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: crimpy and the brain: start to the left on dirty rock to gain the face moving out right over the roof. continue up the less than vertical face on good edges and the occasional jug past a hard move here and there.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: jimson weed: pull through a series of small roofs to gain the slabby headwall. once there, make a series of thoughtful moves, culminating in an awkward lunge for the chains. short but varied!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: mona j: head straight up the bolt line to a short slab, reaching slightly left and straight up for the big crack feature. bear crawl to the right across the top of the feature where you’ll begin to enter a chimney-like adventure. finish with good holds to the right of the chains!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: a brief history of climb: fantastic that goes from easy run-out, to crimpy, to over hanging plates.it stays dry during the rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: the king lives on...: lots of hidden holds and balancy moves

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: no brain, no pain: start with burly moves on good in cut crimps to a large rail then creep past the second bolt which would be best not to miss the clip on. continue up great in cut crimps and jugs to a ledge that you clip the anchors from.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: frontal lobotomy: a tough move off the ledge leads to good holds and much easier climbing for the rest of the route.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: closed project: closed project. a great slab with many of good holds.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: le désespéré: hard move off the ground leads to a good rest and enjoyable climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: murano: follow plates to some balancy movementsthis climb surprisingly stays dry after a light-moderate rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: davinci's left ear: a devious line that will test your 5.10 climbing skills. start below a ledge, left of a large hueco in the wall. work your way up, thinking before acting to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: crude awakening: work your way up some oily (literally) low quality rock and make a surprising move onto a beautiful face.  tip toe up through a number of thoughtful moves to the anchors. considered stout for the grade.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: short by a foot: climb edges and crimpers on a highly featured face to a long move and then a mantle to a ledgeit stays dry during light-moderate rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: red shoes: easy climbing with powerful moves. variable pocket holds with big moves. the top crux has several betas to the anchors that depending on your reach.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: artistic fall: tricky start moves and roof climbing. steepest 5.10 route in the red!?

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: happy trails: foot pain.  tricky face climb with a paucity of holds. plan your sequences carefully.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: all draws and no brains: this route starts with a hard pull over the roof to a couple bolts of easy climbing followed by a big move to terrible hold. finish on easier moves to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Gallery
text: dain bramage: climb a steep featured face for several bolts, to a good rest and an interesting corner system.  get thru the corner and climb thru traversing jugs and steep arete to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Getaway
text: brohemian rhapsody: this route takes on the prominent arete around the left from the main wall. climb on both the left and right side of the arete, using a variety of features to get to the top.   looks like a 4 star climb; climbs like a 2 star climb.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Getaway
text: brohymn: fun but tough route, especially if you don't stay left at the first few bolts to enjoy some nice rests. crux is sustained vertical moves on thin edges. eases up near the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Getaway
text: bridge suite: climb almost all jugs through decent rock up the slightly overhung face. good warm-up.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: chicago style: starts with a right-arching flake feature and climbs some plates and pockets up a mostly clean, vertical wall.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: harshin' my willow: starts up the left-facing flake and gains the ledge via an easy mantle. continue up past pockets, plates, and chickenheads to another cruxy section at the crack feature up high.
feature_tags: crack, crux, flake, ledge, mantle, pocket

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: log skid: start just around the left corner of the wall. climb the vertical face to meet the slab halfway up. figure your way around the arête to a solid stance with no hand holds. test your vertical and pop up to the next hold.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: ballhooter: boulder through the steeper bottom section to a decent rest. straddle the arête then head around left and follow a neat runnel feature to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: shiver me timbhers: short line up big features at the right end of the timber wall with a micro boulder in the middle. stick clip the high first bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: milkin' the stump: start in front of a mound of dirt on good pockets to a punchy boulder, finish with a few long reaches on jugs.jimmy hoctor 10c ;)

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Lumber Yard
text: vermont grade a: this route follows the obvious line of pockets up the far left side of the steep, mostly featureless wall. a few long pulls set you up for a short boulder revolving around your choice of crimps and underclings. enjoy the ride on jugs the rest of the way.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Playground
text: slide: climb knobs and edges to the anchors.  mangy rock down low leads to plain ol' fun above.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Playground
text: tire swing: this is the last route route from the left on the slab wall, just right of slide. begin on the bouldery, somewhat chossy start. climb the slab to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Playground
text: monkey bars: the route begins on a slightly overhanging rock and steepens as you go.  enjoy bigger moves and bigger holds on steeper rock as you near the anchors, great introduction to pulling on steep jug-hauls in the red!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Playground
text: jungle gym: a good route to try if monkey bars went well for you.  enjoy fun climbing on jugs up the every steepening wall.  save a little mojo for the crux mantle at the top!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shipyard
text: kiss the manta ray: this route climbs the pinnacle on good holds. at the top the route traverses left to anchors directly below the summit.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: audie: start in the cave or just to the left of it.  climb up and right to the first bolt.  continue up climbing plates, pockets and a bit of a crack to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: miranda rayne: tackle a longer and slightly harder climb to the right of audie.  climb pockets and flakes past 7 bolts to the anchor.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: bulldozer: boulder up the start of the route to the first bolt.  then work up the slabby face past thought provoking moves to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: significant other: climb past the green start to a ledge.  continue up the face using the occasional horizontal, smear and crimp to the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: haven: there is a small sign at the base of this climb with it's name and grade, i do not know anything else about it.a fun, but slightly squeezed route that climbs up interesting jugs and pockets.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: the g-man: the hardest line on the wall, climbs steeper ground past 6 bolts, just to the left of an arete.  fight the pumpy moves in the middle of the route past slopers and small holds to bigger finishing holds and anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > The Shire
text: k.s.b.: work fun iron edge pulling past long moves on a steep face to a good rest.  move up and left, then traverse right fighting the pump to eventually reach to the large pockets that lead to the finish of the route.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Throwback Crag
text: live music is better: a dirty and difficult start lead to better climbing on iron edges and chicken heads.  it is recommended that you stick clip the first bolt.  the view from the route makes up for the dirty start.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: dura-ace: this long route climbs iron oxide ledges up a slightly less than vertical face. a fun climb to do real quick at the end of the day! no real defined crux just continuously good climbing.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: rail trail: follow a series of ledges and rails up to a bulge around the fourth bolt. slightly slabby

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: over the handlebars: face climbing to a couple of good stances.  route quality should improve as traffic cleans it up a little.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: clips and straps: mostly vertical or slightly slabby with plenty of the typical velo crag ledges and rails until the last two bolts where some technique and style comes in handy.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: lanterne rouge: this route climbs interesting iron oxide features on a vertical to slightly less than vertical face.  start in the crack to the left for the first few bolts. move right to pass the roof on its right side and then pull huge holds to the finish.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: rolling hills: climb through a somewhat chossy but easy start. figure your way through the third and fourth bolt crux. most people trend right here. fun romp to the anchors after that.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: ultegra: a fun route on good crimps up the vertical face to the left of dura-ace.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: tourist attractions: fingery, sustained climbing, makes for a challenging onsight with several cruxes, and feels longer than it is. thought provoking low 10.be safe, wear your helmet!

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: real girls don't pumptrack: starts with some moves on thin holds and heads into an arete. second and third clips are full value.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: the century: chossy start that will benefit quite a bit once some more traffic happens. crux is around the third bolt with some thin moves and a big reach -- options abound in terms of how to cruise this section and your height will dictate how difficult it feels. once past the crux you can have fun cranking on positive holds to the anchor.  near sunset we encountered a plethora, like dozens if not hundreds, of ladybugs on the wall near the anchor, which added to the glee this route provides.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: house of the flying squirrel: bouldery start to a ledge rest. bring an alpine draw/60cm sling/extendable draw(3) for the second bolt if you want to reduce drag. clip the 3rd bolt permadraw from the roof jug, then find amazing features, with sinker jugs, iron bands, and some balancey crimp moves along the way. respect the flying squirrel, if you're lucky enough to meet 'em.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: road rash: huge iron jugs lead to a technical vert/slab crux on micro crimps, followed by thought provoking climbing on varied iron features to a slanted ledge. finish up on a fun, but short lived juggy offwidth to the anchor. actually 75ft. and... we don't use the word "micro" lightly!drys out quick after a rain. sun after 1pm.
feature_tags: crimp, crux, jug, ledge, slab, technical

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: lightning rod arete: from redriverclimbing: afternoon sun. stick clip the first and brave a bit of choss down low, then enjoy thoughtful and balancey climbing to the top. gets some late-afternoon sun.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Velo Crag
text: cheater's trophy loss lament: aka - neil armstrong (lol)a challenging and thought provoking traverse bulge stands as an early crux, leading to an amazing frumpy flake, followed by giant, glorious jugs to the anchor. use the old chain anchor as the last bolt and continue past to the lower-offs on the upper ledge. very climable, but still a bit dirty. will update this when i (or the faist) clean it up fully.gear beta: alpine sling the 4th bolt, and backclean (or alpine sling) the 5th bolt to minimize rope drag.shares first 2 bolts and anchor with the drafter. carefully swing over to use the cleaning perma on the neighboring route to grab the first draws back.north facing, shade all day.does not stay dry in rain.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: first time: this climb starts on top of a rock and immediately traverses right 10' or so to get to your first bolt.  pretty straightforward climb, nothing too extreme (it is a 5.8 after all).  a great view above the trees awaits you at the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: darwin loves you: beging this fun route... good holds followed by a great jug. careful, don't pump out.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: farley's folly: boulder moves on the start to gain the face. head left and up on decent holds. balance back right for the finish. in the early spring the starting holds can get iced over.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: nice to know you: easy first clip followed by a tricky bulge and then rewarding slab climbing above.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: family tradition: fun climb that starts in/near a large crack, sort of runs up the right side of 2 cool parallel curving cracks with a few tricky moves up high.  unfortunately it gets a touch sandy near the top but still very much worth the effort.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: NA

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: pinkies extended: a low crux and steep plates lead to a good rest before a cool boulder problem on pockets and big iron features.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: helping hands: pull through a small overhang to crimps and slabby moves.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: tong shing: crux near the 6th bolt.  trust your body position and statically clip the 6th bolt.  highly technical climb requiring forethought and deliberate maneuvers.  enjoy the crimps and slopers.  bring a squib clip for the first clip, or be sure to spot the climber until clipped.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: generosity: bouldery start on some sandy rock, through a small roof to a huge stance. rest here then head up the overhanging wall with the moves getting less and less straightforward. fight the pump until you hit the final holds and clip the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > Volunteer Wall
text: normalised bramapithecus: reach high for the start holds then surmount a roof to gain the slightly overhanging face.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: threat level blue: watch out for some soft rock, pg13 for getting to high first bolt. may be slightly harder than 5.9

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: weathertop stings: easy climbing to crux at fourth bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: papa piment: get on top of a boulder to start, then find your way through a couple mild bulges. pumpy climbing on pockets and iron fins takes you to the chains.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: no sleep til' campton: great technical line with only a few moves at the grade.  start near a tree at a dip in the trail.  make a long move to get established on the iron horizontals.  clip the first bolt and make the easy moves to the last bolt before the roof.  make a difficult traverse to get established in the groove directly below the roof (crux).  make a tricky reach to pull the roof and enjoy the easy slab to the top.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: kentucky flu: climb the gently sloping face on small holds to a large hueco rest. continue from the hueco out onto a beautiful arete, making use of micro-crimps and knobs as you make your way up this classic route. don't forget to turn around and take in the gorgeous view from the anchors.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: stem cell: step off boulder onto black face, traverse right on small crimps to the arete and go up.  definitely stick clip 1st bolt.

location: Red River Gorge > Pendergrass-Murray Recreational Preserve (PMRP) > What About Bob Wall
text: the speed of enzo: surmount several bulges using mostly pockets and open hand holds on high friction rock.  enjoy a no-hands rest midway up left of the 4th bolt and find the "middle-finger" mono pocket to pull the crux move to the last bolt.  finish right of the last bolt on tufa like formations.

location: Red River Gorge > Southern Region Crags (Misc.) > Hellcat Crag
text: spawn: the crag warm-up.

location: Red River Gorge > Southern Region Crags (Misc.) > Hellcat Crag
text: hell hole: probably the best route on this section of cliff, marked by a unique limonitic (iron banded) hole/tube which goes several feet deep into the rock. this route has also been called "bigfoot's gloryhole."

location: Red River Gorge > Southern Region Crags (Misc.) > Mt. Olive Rock
text: palm friction: a no-feet start leads to less than vertical climbing on plates and edges.  at the 4th bolt the route turns vertical and finishes in a chimney as the holds get smaller and greasier.  remember this is not a gym climb and stem or chimney your way to a fun no-hands anchor clip.
